units.leftText: Now there was a man named Elkanah who was from Ramathaim-zophim in the hill country of Ephraim. He was the son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephraimite.
units.rightText: Now there was a certain man of Ramathaim-zophim, of the hill-country of Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah, the son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephraimite:
leftNotes: 1:1 Or from Ramathaim, a Zuphite; see LXX and 1 Chronicles 6:26|1CH 6:26* and 35.
1:1 Elihu is also called Eliab and Eliel; see 1 Chronicles 6:27|1CH 6:27* and 34.

units.leftText: He had two wives, one named Hannah and the other Peninnah. And Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none.
units.rightText: and he had two wives; the name of the one was Hannah, and the name of the other Peninnah: and Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children.

units.leftText: Year after year Elkanah would go up from his city to worship and sacrifice to the LORD of Hosts at Shiloh, where Eli’s two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were priests to the LORD.
units.rightText: And this man went up out of his city from year to year to worship and to sacrifice unto Jehovah of hosts in Shiloh. And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, priests unto Jehovah, were there.

units.leftText: And whenever the day came for Elkanah to present his sacrifice, he would give portions to his wife Peninnah and to all her sons and daughters.
units.rightText: And when the day came that Elkanah sacrificed, he gave to Peninnah his wife, and to all her sons and her daughters, portions:

units.leftText: But to Hannah he would give a double portion, for he loved her even though the LORD had closed her womb.
units.rightText: but unto Hannah he gave a double portion; for he loved Hannah, but Jehovah had shut up her womb.
leftNotes: 1:5 Or a choice portion

units.leftText: Because the LORD had closed Hannah’s womb, her rival would provoke her viciously to taunt her.
units.rightText: And her rival provoked her sore, to make her fret, because Jehovah had shut up her womb.

units.leftText: And this went on year after year. Whenever Hannah went up to the house of the LORD, her rival taunted her until she wept and would not eat.
units.rightText: And as he did so year by year, when she went up to the house of Jehovah, so she provoked her; therefore she wept, and did not eat.

units.leftText: “Hannah, why are you crying?” her husband Elkanah asked. “Why won’t you eat? Why is your heart so grieved? Am I not better to you than ten sons?” Hannah Prays for a Son
units.rightText: And Elkanah her husband said unto her, Hannah, why weepest thou? and why eatest thou not? and why is thy heart grieved? am not I better to thee than ten sons?

units.leftText: So after they had finished eating and drinking in Shiloh, Hannah stood up. Now Eli the priest was sitting on a chair by the doorpost of the temple of the LORD.
units.rightText: So Hannah rose up after they had eaten in Shiloh, and after they had drunk. Now Eli the priest was sitting upon his seat by the door-post of the temple of Jehovah.

units.leftText: In her bitter distress, Hannah prayed to the LORD and wept with many tears.
units.rightText: And she was in bitterness of soul, and prayed unto Jehovah, and wept sore.

units.leftText: And she made a vow, saying, “O LORD of Hosts, if only You will look upon the affliction of Your maidservant and remember me, not forgetting Your maidservant but giving her a son, then I will dedicate him to the LORD all the days of his life, and no razor shall ever touch his head.”
units.rightText: And she vowed a vow, and said, O Jehovah of hosts, if thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of thy handmaid, and remember me, and not forget thy handmaid, but wilt give unto thy handmaid a man-child, then I will give him unto Jehovah all the days of his life, and there shall no razor come upon his head.

units.leftText: As Hannah kept on praying before the LORD, Eli watched her mouth.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as she continued praying before Jehovah, that Eli marked her mouth.

units.leftText: Hannah was praying in her heart, and though her lips were moving, her voice could not be heard.
units.rightText: Now Hannah, she spake in her heart; only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard: therefore Eli thought she had been drunken.

units.leftText: and said to her, “How long will you be drunk? Put away your wine!”
units.rightText: And Eli said unto her, How long wilt thou be drunken? put away thy wine from thee.

units.leftText: “No, my lord,” Hannah replied. “I am a woman troubled in spirit. I have not had any wine or strong drink, but I have poured out my soul before the LORD.
units.rightText: And Hannah answered and said, No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit: I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but I poured out my soul before Jehovah.

units.leftText: Do not take your servant for a wicked woman, for all this time I have been praying out of the depth of my anguish and grief.”
units.rightText: Count not thy handmaid for a wicked woman; for out of the abundance of my complaint and my provocation have I spoken hitherto.

units.leftText: “Go in peace,” Eli replied, “and may the God of Israel grant the petition you have asked of Him.”
units.rightText: Then Eli answered and said, Go in peace; and the God of Israel grant thy petition that thou hast asked of him.

units.leftText: “May your maidservant find favor with you,” said Hannah. Then she went on her way, and she began to eat, and her face was no longer downcast. The Birth of Samuel
units.rightText: And she said, Let thy handmaid find favor in thy sight. So the woman went her way, and did eat; and her countenance was no more sad.

units.leftText: The next morning they got up early to bow in worship before the LORD, and then they returned home to Ramah.
units.rightText: And they rose up in the morning early, and worshipped before Jehovah, and returned, and came to their house to Ramah. And Elkanah knew Hannah his wife; and Jehovah remembered her;

units.leftText: So in the course of time, Hannah conceived and gave birth to a son. She named him Samuel, saying, “Because I have asked for him from the LORD.”
units.rightText: and it came to pass, when the time was come about, that Hannah conceived, and bare a son; and she called his name Samuel, saying, Because I have asked him of Jehovah.
leftNotes: 1:20 Samuel sounds like the Hebrew for heard of God.

units.leftText: Then Elkanah and all his house went up to make the annual sacrifice to the LORD and to fulfill his vow,
units.rightText: And the man Elkanah, and all his house, went up to offer unto Jehovah the yearly sacrifice, and his vow.

units.leftText: but Hannah did not go. “After the boy is weaned,” she said to her husband, “I will take him to appear before the LORD and to stay there permanently.”
units.rightText: But Hannah went not up; for she said unto her husband, I will not go up until the child be weaned; and then I will bring him, that he may appear before Jehovah, and there abide for ever.
leftNotes: 1:22 MT; DSS include I will offer him as a Nazirite for all time.

units.leftText: “Do what you think is best,” her husband Elkanah replied, “and stay here until you have weaned him. Only may the LORD confirm His word.” So Hannah stayed and nursed her son until she had weaned him.
units.rightText: And Elkanah her husband said unto her, Do what seemeth thee good; tarry until thou have weaned him; only Jehovah establish his word. So the woman tarried and gave her son suck, until she weaned him.
leftNotes: 1:23 MT; DSS, LXX, and Syriac your word

units.leftText: Once she had weaned him, Hannah took the boy with her, along with a three-year-old bull, an ephah of flour, and a skin of wine. Though the boy was still young, she brought him to the house of the LORD at Shiloh.
units.rightText: And when she had weaned him, she took him up with her, with three bullocks, and one ephah of meal, and a bottle of wine, and brought him unto the house of Jehovah in Shiloh: and the child was young.
leftNotes: 1:24 DSS, LXX, and Syriac; MT three bulls
1:24 An ephah is approximately 20 dry quarts or 22 liters (probably about 25.5 pounds or 11.6 kilograms of flour).

units.leftText: And when they had slaughtered the bull, they brought the boy to Eli.
units.rightText: And they slew the bullock, and brought the child to Eli.

units.leftText: “Please, my lord,” said Hannah, “as surely as you live, my lord, I am the woman who stood here beside you praying to the LORD.
units.rightText: And she said, Oh, my lord, as thy soul liveth, my lord, I am the woman that stood by thee here, praying unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: I prayed for this boy, and since the LORD has granted me what I asked of Him,
units.rightText: For this child I prayed; and Jehovah hath given me my petition which I asked of him:

units.leftText: I now dedicate the boy to the LORD. For as long as he lives, he is dedicated to the LORD.” So they worshiped the LORD there.
units.rightText: therefore also I have granted him to Jehovah; as long as he liveth he is granted to Jehovah. And he worshipped Jehovah there.
leftNotes: 1:28 One DSS manuscript; MT he worshiped

units.leftText: At that time Hannah prayed: “My heart rejoices in the LORD; my horn is exalted in the LORD. My mouth speaks boldly against my enemies, for I rejoice in Your salvation.
units.rightText: And Hannah prayed, and said: My heart exulteth in Jehovah; My horn is exalted in Jehovah; My mouth is enlarged over mine enemies; Because I rejoice in thy salvation.
leftNotes: 2:1 Or strength; also in verse 10

units.leftText: There is no one holy like the LORD. Indeed, there is no one besides You! And there is no Rock like our God.
units.rightText: There is none holy as Jehovah; For there is none besides thee, Neither is there any rock like our God.

units.leftText: Do not boast so proudly, or let arrogance come from your mouth, for the LORD is a God who knows, and by Him actions are weighed.
units.rightText: Talk no more so exceeding proudly; Let not arrogancy come out of your mouth; For Jehovah is a God of knowledge, And by him actions are weighed.

units.leftText: The bows of the mighty are broken, but the feeble are equipped with strength.
units.rightText: The bows of the mighty men are broken; And they that stumbled are girded with strength.

units.leftText: The well-fed hire themselves out for food, but the starving hunger no more. The barren woman gives birth to seven, but she who has many sons pines away.
units.rightText: They that were full have hired out themselves for bread; And they that were hungry have ceased to hunger: Yea, the barren hath borne seven; And she that hath many children languisheth.

units.leftText: The LORD brings death and gives life; He brings down to Sheol and raises up.
units.rightText: Jehovah killeth, and maketh alive: He bringeth down to Sheol, and bringeth up.

units.leftText: The LORD sends poverty and wealth; He humbles and He exalts.
units.rightText: Jehovah maketh poor, and maketh rich: He bringeth low, he also lifteth up.

units.leftText: He raises the poor from the dust and lifts the needy from the ash heap. He seats them among princes and bestows on them a throne of honor. For the foundations of the earth are the LORD’s, and upon them He has set the world.
units.rightText: He raiseth up the poor out of the dust, He lifteth up the needy from the dunghill, To make them sit with princes, And inherit the throne of glory: For the pillars of the earth are Jehovah’s, And he hath set the world upon them.

units.leftText: He guards the steps of His faithful ones, but the wicked perish in darkness; for by his own strength shall no man prevail.
units.rightText: He will keep the feet of his holy ones; But the wicked shall be put to silence in darkness; For by strength shall no man prevail.

units.leftText: Those who oppose the LORD will be shattered. He will thunder from heaven against them. The LORD will judge the ends of the earth and will give power to His king. He will exalt the horn of His anointed.”
units.rightText: They that strive with Jehovah shall be broken to pieces; Against them will he thunder in heaven: Jehovah will judge the ends of the earth; And he will give strength unto his king, And exalt the horn of his anointed.

units.leftText: Then Elkanah went home to Ramah, but the boy began ministering to the LORD before Eli the priest. Eli’s Wicked Sons
units.rightText: And Elkanah went to Ramah to his house. And the child did minister unto Jehovah before Eli the priest.

units.leftText: Now the sons of Eli were wicked men; they had no regard for the LORD
units.rightText: Now the sons of Eli were base men; they knew not Jehovah.

units.leftText: or for the custom of the priests with the people.
units.rightText: And the custom of the priests with the people was, that, when any man offered sacrifice, the priest’s servant came, while the flesh was boiling, with a flesh-hook of three teeth in his hand;

units.leftText: and plunge it into the pan or kettle or cauldron or cooking pot. And the priest would claim for himself whatever the meat fork brought up. This is how they treated all the Israelites who came to Shiloh.
units.rightText: and he struck it into the pan, or kettle, or caldron, or pot; all that the flesh-hook brought up the priest took therewith. So they did in Shiloh unto all the Israelites that came thither.

units.leftText: Even before the fat was burned, the servant of the priest would come and say to the man who was sacrificing, “Give the priest some meat to roast, because he will not accept boiled meat from you, but only raw.”
units.rightText: Yea, before they burnt the fat, the priest’s servant came, and said to the man that sacrificed, Give flesh to roast for the priest; for he will not have boiled flesh of thee, but raw.

units.leftText: And if any man said to him, “The fat must be burned first; then you may take whatever you want,” the servant would reply, “No, you must give it to me right now. If you refuse, I will take it by force!”
units.rightText: And if the man said unto him, They will surely burn the fat first, and then take as much as thy soul desireth; then he would say, Nay, but thou shalt give it me now: and if not, I will take it by force.

units.leftText: Thus the sin of these young men was severe in the sight of the LORD, for they were treating the LORD’s offering with contempt.
units.rightText: And the sin of the young men was very great before Jehovah; for the men despised the offering of Jehovah.
leftNotes: 2:17 DSS and LXX; MT men

units.leftText: Now Samuel was ministering before the LORD — a boy wearing a linen ephod.
units.rightText: But Samuel ministered before Jehovah, being a child, girded with a linen ephod.

units.leftText: Each year his mother would make him a little robe and bring it to him when she went with her husband to offer the annual sacrifice.
units.rightText: Moreover his mother made him a little robe, and brought it to him from year to year, when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.

units.leftText: And Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife, saying, “May the LORD give you children by this woman in place of the one she dedicated to the LORD. ” Then they would go home.
units.rightText: And Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife, and said, Jehovah give thee seed of this woman for the petition which was asked of Jehovah. And they went unto their own home.
leftNotes: 2:20 DSS; MT in place of the one requested from the LORD

units.leftText: So the LORD attended to Hannah, and she conceived and gave birth to three sons and two daughters. Meanwhile, the boy Samuel grew up in the presence of the LORD.
units.rightText: And Jehovah visited Hannah, and she conceived, and bare three sons and two daughters. And the child Samuel grew before Jehovah.

units.leftText: Now Eli was very old, and he heard about everything his sons were doing to all Israel and how they were sleeping with the women who served at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: Now Eli was very old; and he heard all that his sons did unto all Israel, and how that they lay with the women that did service at the door of the tent of meeting.

units.leftText: “Why are you doing these things?” Eli said to his sons. “I hear about your wicked deeds from all these people.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Why do ye such things? for I hear of your evil dealings from all this people.

units.leftText: No, my sons; it is not a good report I hear circulating among the LORD’s people.
units.rightText: Nay, my sons; for it is no good report that I hear: ye make Jehovah’s people to transgress.

units.leftText: If a man sins against another man, God can intercede for him; but if a man sins against the LORD, who can intercede for him?” But they would not listen to their father, since the LORD intended to put them to death.
units.rightText: If one man sin against another, God shall judge him; but if a man sin against Jehovah, who shall entreat for him? Notwithstanding, they hearkened not unto the voice of their father, because Jehovah was minded to slay them.
leftNotes: 2:25 Or the judges

units.leftText: And the boy Samuel continued to grow in stature and in favor with the LORD and with man. A Prophecy against the House of Eli
units.rightText: And the child Samuel grew on, and increased in favor both with Jehovah, and also with men.

units.leftText: Then a man of God came to Eli and told him, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Did I not clearly reveal Myself to your father’s house when they were in Egypt under Pharaoh’s house?
units.rightText: And there came a man of God unto Eli, and said unto him, Thus saith Jehovah, Did I reveal myself unto the house of thy father, when they were in Egypt in bondage to Pharaoh’s house?

units.leftText: And out of all the tribes of Israel I selected your father to be My priest, to offer sacrifices on My altar, to burn incense, and to wear an ephod in My presence. I also gave to the house of your father all the food offerings of the Israelites.
units.rightText: and did I choose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to go up unto mine altar, to burn incense, to wear an ephod before me? and did I give unto the house of thy father all the offerings of the children of Israel made by fire?

units.leftText: Why then do you kick at My sacrifice and offering that I have prescribed for My dwelling place? You have honored your sons more than Me by fattening yourselves with the best of all the offerings of My people Israel.’
units.rightText: Wherefore kick ye at my sacrifice and at mine offering, which I have commanded in my habitation, and honorest thy sons above me, to make yourselves fat with the chiefest of all the offerings of Israel my people?
leftNotes: 2:29 Or scorn

units.leftText: Therefore, the LORD, the God of Israel, declares: ‘I did indeed say that your house and the house of your father would walk before Me forever. But now the LORD declares: Far be it from Me! For I will honor those who honor Me, but those who despise Me will be disdained.
units.rightText: Therefore Jehovah, the God of Israel, saith, I said indeed that thy house, and the house of thy father, should walk before me for ever: but now Jehovah saith, Be it far from me; for them that honor me I will honor, and they that despise me shall be lightly esteemed.

units.leftText: Behold, the days are coming when I will cut off your strength and the strength of your father’s house, so that no one in it will reach old age.
units.rightText: Behold, the days come, that I will cut off thine arm, and the arm of thy father’s house, that there shall not be an old man in thy house.

units.leftText: You will see distress in My dwelling place. Despite all that is good in Israel, no one in your house will ever again reach old age.
units.rightText: And thou shalt behold the affliction of my habitation, in all the wealth which God shall give Israel; and there shall not be an old man in thy house for ever.

units.leftText: And every one of you that I do not cut off from My altar, I will cause your eyes to fail and your heart to grieve. All your descendants will die by the sword of men.
units.rightText: And the man of thine, whom I shall not cut off from mine altar, shall be to consume thine eyes, and to grieve thy heart; and all the increase of thy house shall die in the flower of their age.
leftNotes: 2:33 Hebrew; LXX his eyes will fail and his heart will grieve
2:33 Or increase
2:33 DSS and LXX; MT will die as mortals or will die in the prime of life

units.leftText: And this sign shall come to you concerning your two sons Hophni and Phinehas: They will both die on the same day.
units.rightText: And this shall be the sign unto thee, that shall come upon thy two sons, on Hophni and Phinehas: in one day they shall die both of them.

units.leftText: Then I will raise up for Myself a faithful priest. He will do whatever is in My heart and mind. And I will build for him an enduring house, and he will walk before My anointed one for all time.
units.rightText: And I will raise me up a faithful priest, that shall do according to that which is in my heart and in my mind: and I will build him a sure house; and he shall walk before mine anointed for ever.

units.leftText: And everyone left in your house will come and bow down to him for a piece of silver or a morsel of bread, pleading, “Please appoint me to some priestly office so that I can eat a piece of bread.”’”
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, that every one that is left in thy house shall come and bow down to him for a piece of silver and a loaf of bread, and shall say, Put me, I pray thee, into one of the priests’ offices, that I may eat a morsel of bread.

units.leftText: And the boy Samuel ministered to the LORD before Eli.
units.rightText: And the child Samuel ministered unto Jehovah before Eli. And the word of Jehovah was precious in those days; there was no frequent vision.

units.leftText: And at that time Eli, whose eyesight had grown so dim that he could not see, was lying in his room.
units.rightText: And it came to pass at that time, when Eli was laid down in his place (now his eyes had begun to wax dim, so that he could not see),

units.leftText: Before the lamp of God had gone out, Samuel was lying down in the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was located.
units.rightText: and the lamp of God was not yet gone out, and Samuel was laid down to sleep, in the temple of Jehovah, where the ark of God was;

units.leftText: Then the LORD called to Samuel, and he answered, “Here I am.”
units.rightText: that Jehovah called Samuel: and he said, Here am I.

units.leftText: He ran to Eli and said, “Here I am, for you have called me.” “I did not call,” Eli replied. “Go back and lie down.” So he went and lay down.
units.rightText: And he ran unto Eli, and said, Here am I; for thou calledst me. And he said, I called not; lie down again. And he went and lay down.

units.leftText: Once again the LORD called, “Samuel!” So Samuel got up, went to Eli, and said, “Here I am, for you have called me.” “My son, I did not call,” Eli replied. “Go back and lie down.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah called yet again, Samuel. And Samuel arose and went to Eli, and said, Here am I; for thou calledst me. And he answered, I called not, my son; lie down again.

units.leftText: Now Samuel did not yet know the LORD, because the word of the LORD had not yet been revealed to him.
units.rightText: Now Samuel did not yet know Jehovah, neither was the word of Jehovah yet revealed unto him.

units.leftText: Once again, for the third time, the LORD called to Samuel. He got up, went to Eli, and said, “Here I am, for you have called me.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah called Samuel again the third time. And he arose and went to Eli, and said, Here am I; for thou calledst me. And Eli perceived that Jehovah had called the child.

units.leftText: “Go and lie down,” he said to Samuel, “and if He calls you, say, ‘Speak, LORD, for Your servant is listening.’” So Samuel went and lay down in his place.
units.rightText: Therefore Eli said unto Samuel, Go, lie down: and it shall be, if he call thee, that thou shalt say, Speak, Jehovah; for thy servant heareth. So Samuel went and lay down in his place.

units.leftText: Then the LORD came and stood there, calling as before, “Samuel! Samuel!” And Samuel answered, “Speak, for Your servant is listening.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah came, and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. Then Samuel said, Speak; for thy servant heareth.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Samuel, “I am about to do something in Israel at which the ears of all who hear it will tingle.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said to Samuel, Behold, I will do a thing in Israel, at which both the ears of every one that heareth it shall tingle.

units.leftText: On that day I will carry out against Eli everything I have spoken about his house, from beginning to end.
units.rightText: In that day I will perform against Eli all that I have spoken concerning his house, from the beginning even unto the end.

units.leftText: I told him that I would judge his house forever for the iniquity of which he knows, because his sons blasphemed God and he did not restrain them.
units.rightText: For I have told him that I will judge his house for ever, for the iniquity which he knew, because his sons did bring a curse upon themselves, and he restrained them not.
leftNotes: 3:13 LXX; Hebrew made themselves contemptible

units.leftText: Therefore I have sworn to the house of Eli, ‘The iniquity of Eli’s house shall never be atoned for by sacrifice or offering.’” Samuel Shares the Vision
units.rightText: And therefore I have sworn unto the house of Eli, that the iniquity of Eli’s house shall not be expiated with sacrifice nor offering for ever.

units.leftText: Samuel lay down until the morning; then he opened the doors of the house of the LORD. He was afraid to tell Eli the vision,
units.rightText: And Samuel lay until the morning, and opened the doors of the house of Jehovah. And Samuel feared to show Eli the vision.

units.leftText: but Eli called to him and said, “Samuel, my son.” “Here I am,” answered Samuel.
units.rightText: Then Eli called Samuel, and said, Samuel, my son. And he said, Here am I.

units.leftText: “What was the message He gave you?” Eli asked. “Do not hide it from me. May God punish you, and ever so severely, if you hide from me anything He said to you.”
units.rightText: And he said, What is the thing that Jehovah hath spoken unto thee? I pray thee, hide it not from me: God do so to thee, and more also, if thou hide anything from me of all the things that he spake unto thee.

units.leftText: So Samuel told him everything and did not hide a thing from him. “He is the LORD,” replied Eli. “Let Him do what is good in His eyes.”
units.rightText: And Samuel told him every whit, and hid nothing from him. And he said, It is Jehovah: let him do what seemeth him good.

units.leftText: And Samuel grew, and the LORD was with him, and He let none of Samuel’s words fall to the ground.
units.rightText: And Samuel grew, and Jehovah was with him, and did let none of his words fall to the ground.

units.leftText: So all Israel from Dan to Beersheba knew that Samuel was confirmed as a prophet of the LORD.
units.rightText: And all Israel from Dan even to Beer-sheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of Jehovah.

units.leftText: And the LORD continued to appear at Shiloh, because there He revealed Himself to Samuel by His word.
units.rightText: And Jehovah appeared again in Shiloh; for Jehovah revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh by the word of Jehovah.

units.leftText: Thus the word of Samuel came to all Israel.
units.rightText: And the word of Samuel came to all Israel. Now Israel went out against the Philistines to battle, and encamped beside Eben-ezer: and the Philistines encamped in Aphek.

units.leftText: The Philistines arrayed themselves against Israel, and as the battle spread, Israel was defeated by the Philistines, who struck down about four thousand men on the battlefield.
units.rightText: And the Philistines put themselves in array against Israel: and when they joined battle, Israel was smitten before the Philistines; and they slew of the army in the field about four thousand men.

units.leftText: When the troops returned to the camp, the elders of Israel asked, “Why has the LORD brought defeat on us before the Philistines today? Let us bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Shiloh, so that it may go with us to save us from the hand of our enemies.”
units.rightText: And when the people were come into the camp, the elders of Israel said, Wherefore hath Jehovah smitten us to-day before the Philistines? Let us fetch the ark of the covenant of Jehovah out of Shiloh unto us, that it may come among us, and save us out of the hand of our enemies.
leftNotes: 4:3 Or He may go

units.leftText: So the people sent men to Shiloh, and they brought back the ark of the covenant of the LORD of Hosts, who sits enthroned between the cherubim. And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God.
units.rightText: So the people sent to Shiloh; and they brought from thence the ark of the covenant of Jehovah of hosts, who sitteth above the cherubim: and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God.

units.leftText: When the ark of the covenant of the LORD entered the camp, all the Israelites raised such a great shout that the ground shook.
units.rightText: And when the ark of the covenant of Jehovah came into the camp, all Israel shouted with a great shout, so that the earth rang again.

units.leftText: On hearing the noise of the shout, the Philistines asked, “What is this loud shouting in the camp of the Hebrews?”
units.rightText: And when the Philistines heard the noise of the shout, they said, What meaneth the noise of this great shout in the camp of the Hebrews? And they understood that the ark of Jehovah was come into the camp.

units.leftText: the Philistines were afraid. “The gods have entered their camp!” they said. “Woe to us, for nothing like this has happened before.
units.rightText: And the Philistines were afraid, for they said, God is come into the camp. And they said, Woe unto us! for there hath not been such a thing heretofore.
leftNotes: 4:7 Or A god has entered

units.leftText: Woe to us! Who will deliver us from the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods who struck the Egyptians with all kinds of plagues in the wilderness.
units.rightText: Woe unto us! who shall deliver us out of the hand of these mighty gods? these are the gods that smote the Egyptians with all manner of plagues in the wilderness.

units.leftText: Take courage and be men, O Philistines! Otherwise, you will serve the Hebrews just as they served you. Now be men and fight!”
units.rightText: Be strong, and quit yourselves like men, O ye Philistines, that ye be not servants unto the Hebrews, as they have been to you: quit yourselves like men, and fight.

units.leftText: So the Philistines fought, and Israel was defeated, and each man fled to his tent. The slaughter was very great — thirty thousand foot soldiers of Israel fell.
units.rightText: And the Philistines fought, and Israel was smitten, and they fled every man to his tent: and there was a very great slaughter; for there fell of Israel thirty thousand footmen.

units.leftText: The ark of God was captured, and Eli’s two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, died. The Death of Eli
units.rightText: And the ark of God was taken; and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were slain.

units.leftText: That same day a Benjamite ran from the battle line all the way to Shiloh, with his clothes torn and dirt on his head.
units.rightText: And there ran a man of Benjamin out of the army, and came to Shiloh the same day, with his clothes rent, and with earth upon his head.

units.leftText: When he arrived, there was Eli, sitting on his chair beside the road and watching, because his heart trembled for the ark of God. When the man entered the city to give a report, the whole city cried out.
units.rightText: And when he came, lo, Eli was sitting upon his seat by the wayside watching; for his heart trembled for the ark of God. And when the man came into the city, and told it, all the city cried out.

units.leftText: Eli heard the outcry and asked, “Why this commotion?”
units.rightText: And when Eli heard the noise of the crying, he said, What meaneth the noise of this tumult? And the man hasted, and came and told Eli.

units.leftText: Now Eli was ninety-eight years old, and his gaze was fixed because he could not see.
units.rightText: Now Eli was ninety and eight years old; and his eyes were set, so that he could not see.

units.leftText: “I have just come from the battle,” the man said to Eli. “I fled from there today.” “What happened, my son?” Eli asked.
units.rightText: And the man said unto Eli, I am he that came out of the army, and I fled to-day out of the army. And he said, How went the matter, my son?

units.leftText: The messenger answered, “Israel has fled before the Philistines, and there has been a great slaughter among the people. Your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are both dead, and the ark of God has been captured.”
units.rightText: And he that brought the tidings answered and said, Israel is fled before the Philistines, and there hath been also a great slaughter among the people, and thy two sons also, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead, and the ark of God is taken.

units.leftText: As soon as the ark of God was mentioned, Eli fell backward from his chair by the city gate, and being old and heavy, he broke his neck and died. And Eli had judged Israel forty years.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when he made mention of the ark of God, that Eli fell from off his seat backward by the side of the gate; and his neck brake, and he died: for he was an old man, and heavy. And he had judged Israel forty years.
leftNotes: 4:18 Or governed or led

units.leftText: Now Eli’s daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was pregnant and about to give birth. When she heard the news of the capture of God’s ark and the deaths of her father-in-law and her husband, she collapsed and gave birth, for her labor pains overtook her.
units.rightText: And his daughter-in-law, Phinehas’ wife, was with child, near to be delivered: and when she heard the tidings that the ark of God was taken, and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she bowed herself and brought forth; for her pains came upon her.

units.leftText: As she was dying, the women attending to her said, “Do not be afraid, for you have given birth to a son!”
units.rightText: And about the time of her death the women that stood by her said unto her, Fear not; for thou hast brought forth a son. But she answered not, neither did she regard it.

units.leftText: And she named the boy Ichabod, saying, “The glory has departed from Israel,” because the ark of God had been captured and her father-in-law and her husband had been killed.
units.rightText: And she named the child Ichabod, saying, The glory is departed from Israel; because the ark of God was taken, and because of her father-in-law and her husband.
leftNotes: 4:21 Ichabod means no glory.
4:21 Or gone into exile; also in verse 22

units.leftText: “The glory has departed from Israel,” she said, “for the ark of God has been captured.”
units.rightText: And she said, The glory is departed from Israel; for the ark of God is taken.

units.leftText: After the Philistines had captured the ark of God, they took it from Ebenezer to Ashdod,
units.rightText: Now the Philistines had taken the ark of God, and they brought it from Eben-ezer unto Ashdod.

units.leftText: carried it into the temple of Dagon, and set it beside his statue.
units.rightText: And the Philistines took the ark of God, and brought it into the house of Dagon, and set it by Dagon.
leftNotes: 5:2 Literally set it beside Dagon

units.leftText: When the people of Ashdod got up early the next morning, there was Dagon, fallen on his face before the ark of the LORD. So they took Dagon and returned him to his place.
units.rightText: And when they of Ashdod arose early on the morrow, behold, Dagon was fallen upon his face to the ground before the ark of Jehovah. And they took Dagon, and set him in his place again.

units.leftText: But when they got up early the next morning, there was Dagon, fallen on his face before the ark of the LORD, with his head and his hands broken off and lying on the threshold. Only the torso remained.
units.rightText: And when they arose early on the morrow morning, behold, Dagon was fallen upon his face to the ground before the ark of Jehovah; and the head of Dagon and both the palms of his hands lay cut off upon the threshold; only the stump of Dagon was left to him.

units.leftText: That is why, to this day, the priests of Dagon and all who enter the temple of Dagon in Ashdod do not step on the threshold.
units.rightText: Therefore neither the priests of Dagon, nor any that come into Dagon’s house, tread on the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod, unto this day.

units.leftText: Now the hand of the LORD was heavy on the people of Ashdod and its vicinity, ravaging them and afflicting them with tumors.
units.rightText: But the hand of Jehovah was heavy upon them of Ashdod, and he destroyed them, and smote them with tumors, even Ashdod and the borders thereof.
leftNotes: 5:6 Hebrew; LXX and Vulgate include And rats appeared in their land, and death and destruction were throughout the city.

units.leftText: And when the men of Ashdod saw what was happening, they said, “The ark of the God of Israel must not stay here with us, because His hand is heavy upon us and upon our god Dagon.”
units.rightText: And when the men of Ashdod saw that it was so, they said, The ark of the God of Israel shall not abide with us; for his hand is sore upon us, and upon Dagon our god.

units.leftText: So they called together all the rulers of the Philistines and asked, “What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel?” “It must be moved to Gath,” they replied. So they carried away the ark of the God of Israel.
units.rightText: They sent therefore and gathered all the lords of the Philistines unto them, and said, What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel? And they answered, Let the ark of the God of Israel be carried about unto Gath. And they carried the ark of the God of Israel thither.

units.leftText: But after they had moved the ark to Gath, the LORD’s hand was also against that city, throwing it into great confusion and afflicting the men of the city, both young and old, with an outbreak of tumors.
units.rightText: And it was so, that, after they had carried it about, the hand of Jehovah was against the city with a very great discomfiture: and he smote the men of the city, both small and great; and tumors brake out upon them.

units.leftText: So they sent the ark of God to Ekron, but as it arrived, the Ekronites cried out, “They have brought us the ark of the God of Israel in order to kill us and our people!”
units.rightText: So they sent the ark of God to Ekron. And it came to pass, as the ark of God came to Ekron, that the Ekronites cried out, saying, They have brought about the ark of the God of Israel to us, to slay us and our people.

units.leftText: Then the Ekronites called together all the rulers of the Philistines and said, “Send away the ark of the God of Israel. It must return to its place, so that it will not kill us and our people!”
units.rightText: They sent therefore and gathered together all the lords of the Philistines, and they said, Send away the ark of the God of Israel, and let it go again to its own place, that it slay us not, and our people. For there was a deadly discomfiture throughout all the city; the hand of God was very heavy there.
leftNotes: 5:11 Or He will not

units.leftText: Those who did not die were afflicted with tumors, and the outcry of the city went up to heaven.
units.rightText: And the men that died not were smitten with the tumors; and the cry of the city went up to heaven.

units.leftText: When the ark of the LORD had been in the land of the Philistines seven months,
units.rightText: And the ark of Jehovah was in the country of the Philistines seven months.

units.leftText: the Philistines summoned the priests and diviners, saying, “What shall we do with the ark of the LORD? Tell us how to send it back to its place.”
units.rightText: And the Philistines called for the priests and the diviners, saying, What shall we do with the ark of Jehovah? show us wherewith we shall send it to its place.

units.leftText: They replied, “If you return the ark of the God of Israel, do not send it away empty, but by all means return it to Him with a guilt offering. Then you will be healed, and you will understand why His hand has not been lifted from you.”
units.rightText: And they said, If ye send away the ark of the God of Israel, send it not empty; but by all means return him a trespass-offering: then ye shall be healed, and it shall be known to you why his hand is not removed from you.

units.leftText: “What guilt offering should we send back to Him?” asked the Philistines.
units.rightText: Then said they, What shall be the trespass-offering which we shall return to him? And they said, Five golden tumors, and five golden mice, according to the number of the lords of the Philistines; for one plague was on you all, and on your lords.

units.leftText: Make images of your tumors and of the rats that are ravaging the land. Give glory to the God of Israel, and perhaps He will lift His hand from you and your gods and your land.
units.rightText: Wherefore ye shall make images of your tumors, and images of your mice that mar the land; and ye shall give glory unto the God of Israel: peradventure he will lighten his hand from off you, and from off your gods, and from off your land.

units.leftText: Why harden your hearts as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened theirs? When He afflicted them, did they not send the people out so they could go on their way?
units.rightText: Wherefore then do ye harden your hearts, as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened their hearts? When he had wrought wonderfully among them, did they not let the people go, and they departed?
leftNotes: 6:6 Or make heavy; similarly again in this verse

units.leftText: Now, therefore, prepare one new cart with two milk cows that have never been yoked. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take their calves away and pen them up.
units.rightText: Now therefore take and prepare you a new cart, and two milch kine, on which there hath come no yoke; and tie the kine to the cart, and bring their calves home from them;

units.leftText: Take the ark of the LORD, set it on the cart, and in a chest beside it put the gold objects you are sending back to Him as a guilt offering.
units.rightText: and take the ark of Jehovah, and lay it upon the cart; and put the jewels of gold, which ye return him for a trespass-offering, in a coffer by the side thereof; and send it away, that it may go.

units.leftText: but keep watching it. If it goes up the road to its homeland, toward Beth-shemesh, it is the LORD who has brought on us this great disaster. But if it does not, then we will know that it was not His hand that punished us and that it happened by chance.”
units.rightText: And see; if it goeth up by the way of its own border to Beth-shemesh, then he hath done us this great evil: but if not, then we shall know that it is not his hand that smote us; it was a chance that happened to us.

units.leftText: So the men did as instructed. They took two milk cows, hitched them to the cart, and penned up their calves.
units.rightText: And the men did so, and took two milch kine, and tied them to the cart, and shut up their calves at home;

units.leftText: Then they put the ark of the LORD on the cart, along with the chest containing the gold rats and the images of the tumors.
units.rightText: and they put the ark of Jehovah upon the cart, and the coffer with the mice of gold and the images of their tumors.

units.leftText: And the cows headed straight up the road toward Beth-shemesh, staying on that one highway and lowing as they went, never straying to the right or to the left. The rulers of the Philistines followed behind them to the border of Beth-shemesh.
units.rightText: And the kine took the straight way by the way to Beth-shemesh; they went along the highway, lowing as they went, and turned not aside to the right hand or to the left; and the lords of the Philistines went after them unto the border of Beth-shemesh.

units.leftText: Now the people of Beth-shemesh were harvesting wheat in the valley, and when they looked up and saw the ark, they were overjoyed at the sight.
units.rightText: And they of Beth-shemesh were reaping their wheat harvest in the valley; and they lifted up their eyes, and saw the ark, and rejoiced to see it.

units.leftText: The cart came to the field of Joshua of Beth-shemesh and stopped there near a large rock. The people chopped up the cart and offered the cows as a burnt offering to the LORD.
units.rightText: And the cart came into the field of Joshua the Beth-shemite, and stood there, where there was a great stone: and they clave the wood of the cart, and offered up the kine for a burnt-offering unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: And the Levites took down the ark of the LORD and the chest containing the gold objects, and they placed them on the large rock. That day the men of Beth-shemesh offered burnt offerings and made sacrifices to the LORD.
units.rightText: And the Levites took down the ark of Jehovah, and the coffer that was with it, wherein the jewels of gold were, and put them on the great stone: and the men of Beth-shemesh offered burnt-offerings and sacrificed sacrifices the same day unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: And when the five rulers of the Philistines saw this, they returned to Ekron that same day.
units.rightText: And when the five lords of the Philistines had seen it, they returned to Ekron the same day.

units.leftText: As a guilt offering to the LORD, the Philistines had sent back one gold tumor for each city: Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron.
units.rightText: And these are the golden tumors which the Philistines returned for a trespass-offering unto Jehovah: for Ashdod one, for Gaza one, for Ashkelon one, for Gath one, for Ekron one;

units.leftText: The number of gold rats also corresponded to the number of Philistine cities belonging to the five rulers — the fortified cities and their outlying villages. And the large rock on which they placed the ark of the LORD stands to this day in the field of Joshua of Beth-shemesh.
units.rightText: and the golden mice, according to the number of all the cities of the Philistines belonging to the five lords, both of fortified cities and of country villages, even unto the great stone, whereon they set down the ark of Jehovah, which stone remaineth unto this day in the field of Joshua the Beth-shemite.
leftNotes: 6:18 Or great meadow; Hebrew Abel-haggedolah

units.leftText: But God struck down some of the people of Beth-shemesh because they looked inside the ark of the LORD. He struck down seventy men, and the people mourned because the LORD had struck them with a great slaughter.
units.rightText: And he smote of the men of Beth-shemesh, because they had looked into the ark of Jehovah, he smote of the people seventy men, and fifty thousand men; and the people mourned, because Jehovah had smitten the people with a great slaughter.
leftNotes: 6:19 A few late Hebrew manuscripts and Josephus; most Hebrew manuscripts 70 men and 50,000 men; LXX 70 men and 50,000 men of the people; Syriac and Arabic 70 men and 5,000 men; alternately, possibly 70 men and 50 oxen

units.leftText: The men of Beth-shemesh asked, “Who can stand in the presence of the LORD, this holy God? To whom should the ark go up from here?”
units.rightText: And the men of Beth-shemesh said, Who is able to stand before Jehovah, this holy God? and to whom shall he go up from us?

units.leftText: So they sent messengers to the people of Kiriath-jearim, saying, “The Philistines have returned the ark of the LORD. Come down and take it up with you.”
units.rightText: And they sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiriath-jearim, saying, The Philistines have brought back the ark of Jehovah; come ye down, and fetch it up to you.

units.leftText: Then the men of Kiriath-jearim came for the ark of the LORD and took it into Abinadab’s house on the hill. And they consecrated his son Eleazar to guard the ark of the LORD.
units.rightText: And the men of Kiriath-jearim came, and fetched up the ark of Jehovah, and brought it into the house of Abinadab in the hill, and sanctified Eleazar his son to keep the ark of Jehovah.

units.leftText: And from that day a long time passed, twenty years in all, as the ark remained at Kiriath-jearim. And all the house of Israel mournfully sought the LORD.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, from the day that the ark abode in Kiriath-jearim, that the time was long; for it was twenty years: and all the house of Israel lamented after Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then Samuel said to all the house of Israel, “If you are returning to the LORD with all your hearts, then put away the foreign gods and Ashtoreths among you, prepare your hearts for the LORD, and serve Him only. And He will deliver you from the hand of the Philistines.”
units.rightText: And Samuel spake unto all the house of Israel, saying, If ye do return unto Jehovah with all your heart, then put away the foreign gods and the Ashtaroth from among you, and direct your hearts unto Jehovah, and serve him only; and he will deliver you out of the hand of the Philistines.

units.leftText: So the Israelites put away the Baals and Ashtoreths and served only the LORD.
units.rightText: Then the children of Israel did put away the Baalim and the Ashtaroth, and served Jehovah only.

units.leftText: Then Samuel said, “Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray to the LORD on your behalf.”
units.rightText: And Samuel said, Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray for you unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: When they had gathered at Mizpah, they drew water and poured it out before the LORD. On that day they fasted, and there they confessed, “We have sinned against the LORD.” And Samuel judged the Israelites at Mizpah.
units.rightText: And they gathered together to Mizpah, and drew water, and poured it out before Jehovah, and fasted on that day, and said there, We have sinned against Jehovah. And Samuel judged the children of Israel in Mizpah.
leftNotes: 7:6 Or governed or led; similarly in verses 15, 16, and 17

units.leftText: When the Philistines heard that the Israelites had gathered at Mizpah, their rulers marched up toward Israel. And when the Israelites learned of this, they feared the Philistines
units.rightText: And when the Philistines heard that the children of Israel were gathered together to Mizpah, the lords of the Philistines went up against Israel. And when the children of Israel heard it, they were afraid of the Philistines.

units.leftText: and said to Samuel, “Do not stop crying out to the LORD our God for us, that He may save us from the hand of the Philistines.”
units.rightText: And the children of Israel said to Samuel, Cease not to cry unto Jehovah our God for us, that he will save us out of the hand of the Philistines.

units.leftText: Then Samuel took a suckling lamb and offered it as a whole burnt offering to the LORD. He cried out to the LORD on behalf of Israel, and the LORD answered him.
units.rightText: And Samuel took a sucking lamb, and offered it for a whole burnt-offering unto Jehovah: and Samuel cried unto Jehovah for Israel; and Jehovah answered him.

units.leftText: As the Philistines drew near to fight against Israel, Samuel was offering up the burnt offering. But that day the LORD thundered loudly against the Philistines and threw them into such confusion that they fled before Israel.
units.rightText: And as Samuel was offering up the burnt-offering, the Philistines drew near to battle against Israel; but Jehovah thundered with a great thunder on that day upon the Philistines, and discomfited them; and they were smitten down before Israel.

units.leftText: Then the men of Israel charged out of Mizpah and pursued the Philistines, striking them down all the way to an area below Beth-car.
units.rightText: And the men of Israel went out of Mizpah, and pursued the Philistines, and smote them, until they came under Beth-car.

units.leftText: Afterward, Samuel took a stone and set it up between Mizpah and Shen. He named it Ebenezer, saying, “Thus far the LORD has helped us.”
units.rightText: Then Samuel took a stone, and set it between Mizpah and Shen, and called the name of it Eben-ezer, saying, Hitherto hath Jehovah helped us.
leftNotes: 7:12 Hebrew; LXX and Syriac Jeshanah
7:12 Ebenezer means stone of help.

units.leftText: So the Philistines were subdued, and they stopped invading the territory of Israel. And the hand of the LORD was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.
units.rightText: So the Philistines were subdued, and they came no more within the border of Israel: and the hand of Jehovah was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.

units.leftText: The cities from Ekron to Gath, which the Philistines had taken, were restored to Israel, who also delivered the surrounding territory from the hand of the Philistines. And there was peace between the Israelites and the Amorites.
units.rightText: And the cities which the Philistines had taken from Israel were restored to Israel, from Ekron even unto Gath; and the border thereof did Israel deliver out of the hand of the Philistines. And there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.

units.leftText: So Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.
units.rightText: And Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.

units.leftText: Every year he would go on a circuit from Bethel to Gilgal to Mizpah, judging Israel in all these places.
units.rightText: And he went from year to year in circuit to Beth-el, and Gilgal, and Mizpah; and he judged Israel in all those places.

units.leftText: Then he would return to Ramah because his home was there, and there he judged Israel and built an altar to the LORD.
units.rightText: And his return was to Ramah, for there was his house; and there he judged Israel: and he built there an altar unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: When Samuel grew old, he appointed his sons as judges over Israel.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Samuel was old, that he made his sons judges over Israel.
leftNotes: 8:1 Or governors or leaders; similarly in verses 2, 5, 6, and 20

units.leftText: The name of his firstborn son was Joel, and the name of his second was Abijah. They were judges in Beersheba.
units.rightText: Now the name of his first-born was Joel; and the name of his second, Abijah: they were judges in Beer-sheba.

units.leftText: But his sons did not walk in his ways; they turned aside toward dishonest gain, accepting bribes and perverting justice.
units.rightText: And his sons walked not in his ways, but turned aside after lucre, and took bribes, and perverted justice.

units.leftText: So all the elders of Israel gathered together and came to Samuel at Ramah.
units.rightText: Then all the elders of Israel gathered themselves together, and came to Samuel unto Ramah;

units.leftText: “Look,” they said, “you are old, and your sons do not walk in your ways. Now appoint a king to judge us like all the other nations.”
units.rightText: and they said unto him, Behold, thou art old, and thy sons walk not in thy ways: now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.

units.leftText: But when they said, “Give us a king to judge us,” their demand was displeasing in the sight of Samuel; so he prayed to the LORD.
units.rightText: But the thing displeased Samuel, when they said, Give us a king to judge us. And Samuel prayed unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: And the LORD said to Samuel, “Listen to the voice of the people in all that they say to you. For it is not you they have rejected, but they have rejected Me as their king.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Samuel, Hearken unto the voice of the people in all that they say unto thee; for they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not be king over them.

units.leftText: Just as they have done from the day I brought them up out of Egypt until this day, forsaking Me and serving other gods, so they are doing to you.
units.rightText: According to all the works which they have done since the day that I brought them up out of Egypt even unto this day, in that they have forsaken me, and served other gods, so do they also unto thee.

units.leftText: Now listen to their voice; but you must solemnly warn them and show them the manner of the king who will reign over them.” Samuel’s Warning
units.rightText: Now therefore hearken unto their voice: howbeit thou shalt protest solemnly unto them, and shalt show them the manner of the king that shall reign over them.

units.leftText: So Samuel spoke all the words of the LORD to the people who were asking him for a king.
units.rightText: And Samuel told all the words of Jehovah unto the people that asked of him a king.

units.leftText: He said, “This will be the manner of the king who will reign over you: He will take your sons and appoint them to serve his own chariots and horses, and to run in front of his chariots.
units.rightText: And he said, This will be the manner of the king that shall reign over you: he will take your sons, and appoint them unto him, for his chariots, and to be his horsemen; and they shall run before his chariots;

units.leftText: He will appoint some for himself as commanders of thousands and of fifties, and others to plow his ground, to reap his harvest, and to make his weapons of war and equipment for his chariots.
units.rightText: and he will appoint them unto him for captains of thousands, and captains of fifties; and he will set some to plow his ground, and to reap his harvest, and to make his instruments of war, and the instruments of his chariots.

units.leftText: And he will take your daughters to be perfumers, cooks, and bakers.
units.rightText: And he will take your daughters to be perfumers, and to be cooks, and to be bakers.

units.leftText: He will take the best of your fields and vineyards and olive groves and give them to his servants.
units.rightText: And he will take your fields, and your vineyards, and your oliveyards, even the best of them, and give them to his servants.

units.leftText: He will take a tenth of your grain and grape harvest and give it to his officials and servants.
units.rightText: And he will take the tenth of your seed, and of your vineyards, and give to his officers, and to his servants.

units.leftText: And he will take your menservants and maidservants and your best cattle and donkeys and put them to his own use.
units.rightText: And he will take your men-servants, and your maid-servants, and your goodliest young men, and your asses, and put them to his work.
leftNotes: 8:16 LXX; Hebrew your best young men

units.leftText: He will take a tenth of your flocks, and you yourselves will become his slaves.
units.rightText: He will take the tenth of your flocks: and ye shall be his servants.

units.leftText: When that day comes, you will beg for relief from the king you have chosen, but the LORD will not answer you on that day.” God Grants the Request
units.rightText: And ye shall cry out in that day because of your king whom ye shall have chosen you; and Jehovah will not answer you in that day.

units.leftText: Nevertheless , the people refused to listen to Samuel. “No!” they said. “We must have a king over us.
units.rightText: But the people refused to hearken unto the voice of Samuel; and they said, Nay: but we will have a king over us,

units.leftText: Then we will be like all the other nations, with a king to judge us, to go out before us, and to fight our battles.”
units.rightText: that we also may be like all the nations, and that our king may judge us, and go out before us, and fight our battles.

units.leftText: Samuel listened to all the words of the people and repeated them in the hearing of the LORD.
units.rightText: And Samuel heard all the words of the people, and he rehearsed them in the ears of Jehovah.

units.leftText: “Listen to their voice,” the LORD said to Samuel. “Appoint a king for them.” Then Samuel told the men of Israel, “Everyone must go back to his city.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said to Samuel, Hearken unto their voice, and make them a king. And Samuel said unto the men of Israel, Go ye every man unto his city.

units.leftText: Now there was a Benjamite, a powerful man, whose name was Kish son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Becorath, the son of Aphiah of Benjamin.
units.rightText: Now there was a man of Benjamin, whose name was Kish, the son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Becorath, the son of Aphiah, the son of a Benjamite, a mighty man of valor.

units.leftText: And he had a son named Saul, choice and handsome, without equal among the Israelites — a head taller than any of the people.
units.rightText: And he had a son, whose name was Saul, a young man and a goodly: and there was not among the children of Israel a goodlier person than he: from his shoulders and upward he was higher than any of the people.

units.leftText: One day the donkeys of Saul’s father Kish wandered off, and Kish said to his son Saul, “Take one of the servants and go look for the donkeys.”
units.rightText: And the asses of Kish, Saul’s father, were lost. And Kish said to Saul his son, Take now one of the servants with thee, and arise, go seek the asses.

units.leftText: So Saul passed through the hill country of Ephraim and then through the land of Shalishah, but they did not find the donkeys. He and the servant went through the region of Shaalim, but they were not there. Then they went through the land of Benjamin, and still they did not find them.
units.rightText: And he passed through the hill-country of Ephraim, and passed through the land of Shalishah, but they found them not: then they passed through the land of Shaalim, and there they were not: and he passed through the land of the Benjamites, but they found them not.

units.leftText: When they reached the land of Zuph, Saul said to his servant, “Come, let us go back, or my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us.”
units.rightText: When they were come to the land of Zuph, Saul said to his servant that was with him, Come, and let us return, lest my father leave off caring for the asses, and be anxious for us.

units.leftText: “Look,” said the servant, “in this city there is a man of God who is highly respected; everything he says surely comes to pass. Let us go there now. Perhaps he will tell us which way to go.”
units.rightText: And he said unto him, Behold now, there is in this city a man of God, and he is a man that is held in honor; all that he saith cometh surely to pass: now let us go thither; peradventure he can tell us concerning our journey whereon we go.

units.leftText: “If we do go,” Saul replied, “what can we give the man? For the bread in our packs is gone, and there is no gift to take to the man of God. What do we have?”
units.rightText: Then said Saul to his servant, But, behold, if we go, what shall we bring the man? for the bread is spent in our vessels, and there is not a present to bring to the man of God: what have we?

units.leftText: The servant answered him again. “Look,” he said, “I have here in my hand a quarter shekel of silver. I will give it to the man of God, and he will tell us our way.”
units.rightText: And the servant answered Saul again, and said, Behold, I have in my hand the fourth part of a shekel of silver: that will I give to the man of God, to tell us our way.
leftNotes: 9:8 A quarter shekel is approximately 0.1 ounces or 2.85 grams of silver.

units.leftText: (Formerly in Israel, a man on his way to inquire of God would say, “Come, let us go to the seer.” For the prophet of today was formerly called the seer.)
units.rightText: (Beforetime in Israel, when a man went to inquire of God, thus he said, Come, and let us go to the seer; for he that is now called a Prophet was beforetime called a Seer.)

units.leftText: “Good,” said Saul to his servant. “Come, let us go.” So they set out for the city where the man of God was.
units.rightText: Then said Saul to his servant, Well said; come, let us go. So they went unto the city where the man of God was.

units.leftText: And as they were climbing the hill to the city, they met some young women coming out to draw water and asked, “Is the seer here?”
units.rightText: As they went up the ascent to the city, they found young maidens going out to draw water, and said unto them, Is the seer here?

units.leftText: “Yes, he is ahead of you,” they answered. “Hurry now, for today he has come to the city because the people have a sacrifice on the high place.
units.rightText: And they answered them, and said, He is; behold, he is before thee: make haste now, for he is come to-day into the city; for the people have a sacrifice to-day in the high place.

units.leftText: As soon as you enter the city, you will find him before he goes up to the high place to eat. The people will not eat until he comes, because he must bless the sacrifice; after that, the guests will eat. Go up at once; you will find him.”
units.rightText: As soon as ye are come into the city, ye shall straightway find him, before he goeth up to the high place to eat; for the people will not eat until he come, because he doth bless the sacrifice; and afterwards they eat that are bidden. Now therefore get you up; for at this time ye shall find him.

units.leftText: So Saul and his servant went up toward the city, and as they were entering it, there was Samuel coming toward them on his way up to the high place.
units.rightText: And they went up to the city; and as they came within the city, behold, Samuel came out toward them, to go up to the high place.

units.leftText: Now on the day before Saul’s arrival, the LORD had revealed to Samuel,
units.rightText: Now Jehovah had revealed unto Samuel a day before Saul came, saying,

units.leftText: “At this time tomorrow I will send you a man from the land of Benjamin, and you are to anoint him ruler over My people Israel; he will save them from the hand of the Philistines. For I have looked upon My people, because their cry has come to Me.”
units.rightText: To-morrow about this time I will send thee a man out of the land of Benjamin, and thou shalt anoint him to be prince over my people Israel; and he shall save my people out of the hand of the Philistines: for I have looked upon my people, because their cry is come unto me.

units.leftText: When Samuel saw Saul, the LORD told him, “Here is the man of whom I spoke; he shall rule over My people.”
units.rightText: And when Samuel saw Saul, Jehovah said unto him, Behold, the man of whom I spake to thee! this same shall have authority over my people.

units.leftText: Saul approached Samuel in the gateway and asked, “Would you please tell me where the seer’s house is?”
units.rightText: Then Saul drew near to Samuel in the gate, and said, Tell me, I pray thee, where the seer’s house is.

units.leftText: “I am the seer,” Samuel replied. “Go up before me to the high place, for you shall eat with me today. And when I send you off in the morning, I will tell you all that is in your heart.
units.rightText: And Samuel answered Saul, and said, I am the seer; go up before me unto the high place, for ye shall eat with me to-day: and in the morning I will let thee go, and will tell thee all that is in thy heart.

units.leftText: As for the donkeys you lost three days ago, do not worry about them, for they have been found. And upon whom is all the desire of Israel, if not upon you and all your father’s house?”
units.rightText: And as for thine asses that were lost three days ago, set not thy mind on them; for they are found. And for whom is all that is desirable in Israel? Is it not for thee, and for all thy father’s house?

units.leftText: Saul replied, “Am I not a Benjamite from the smallest tribe of Israel, and is not my clan the least of all the clans of Benjamin? So why would you say such a thing to me?”
units.rightText: And Saul answered and said, Am not I a Benjamite, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel? and my family the least of all the families of the tribe of Benjamin? wherefore then speakest thou to me after this manner?

units.leftText: Then Samuel took Saul and his servant, brought them into the hall, and seated them in the place of honor among those who were invited — about thirty in all.
units.rightText: And Samuel took Saul and his servant, and brought them into the guest-chamber, and made them sit in the chiefest place among them that were bidden, who were about thirty persons.

units.leftText: And Samuel said to the cook, “Bring the portion I gave you and told you to set aside.”
units.rightText: And Samuel said unto the cook, Bring the portion which I gave thee, of which I said unto thee, Set it by thee.

units.leftText: So the cook picked up the leg and what was attached to it and set it before Saul. Then Samuel said, “Here is what was kept back. It was set apart for you. Eat, for it has been kept for you for this occasion, from the time I said, ‘I have invited the people.’” So Saul dined with Samuel that day.
units.rightText: And the cook took up the thigh, and that which was upon it, and set it before Saul. And Samuel said, Behold, that which hath been reserved! set it before thee and eat; because unto the appointed time hath it been kept for thee, for I said, I have invited the people. So Saul did eat with Samuel that day.

units.leftText: And after they had come down from the high place into the city, Samuel spoke with Saul on the roof of his house.
units.rightText: And when they were come down from the high place into the city, he communed with Saul upon the housetop.

units.leftText: They got up early in the morning, and just before dawn Samuel called to Saul on the roof, “Get ready, and I will send you on your way!” So Saul got ready, and both he and Samuel went outside together.
units.rightText: And they arose early: and it came to pass about the spring of the day, that Samuel called to Saul on the housetop, saying, Up, that I may send thee away. And Saul arose, and they went out both of them, he and Samuel, abroad.

units.leftText: As they were going down to the edge of the city, Samuel said to Saul, “Tell the servant to go on ahead of us, but you stay for a while, and I will reveal to you the word of God.” So the servant went on.
units.rightText: As they were going down at the end of the city, Samuel said to Saul, Bid the servant pass on before us (and he passed on), but stand thou still first, that I may cause thee to hear the word of God.

units.leftText: Then Samuel took a flask of oil, poured it on Saul’s head, kissed him, and said, “Has not the LORD anointed you ruler over His inheritance?
units.rightText: Then Samuel took the vial of oil, and poured it upon his head, and kissed him, and said, Is it not that Jehovah hath anointed thee to be prince over his inheritance?
leftNotes: 10:1 Hebrew; LXX “Has not the LORD anointed you ruler over Israel? And you will rule over the LORD’s people and save them from their enemies around them. This will be the sign to you that the LORD has appointed you to be leader over His inheritance.

units.leftText: When you leave me today, you will find two men at Rachel’s tomb in Zelzah on the border of Benjamin. They will say to you, ‘The donkeys you seek have been found, and now your father has stopped worrying about the donkeys and started worrying about you, asking, “What should I do about my son?”’
units.rightText: When thou art departed from me to-day, then thou shalt find two men by Rachel’s sepulchre, in the border of Benjamin at Zelzah; and they will say unto thee, The asses which thou wentest to seek are found; and, lo, thy father hath left off caring for the asses, and is anxious for you, saying, What shall I do for my son?

units.leftText: Then you will go on from there until you come to the Oak of Tabor. Three men going up to God at Bethel will meet you there, one carrying three young goats, another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a skin of wine.
units.rightText: Then shalt thou go on forward from thence, and thou shalt come to the oak of Tabor; and there shall meet thee there three men going up to God to Beth-el, one carrying three kids, and another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a bottle of wine:
leftNotes: 10:3 Or Terebinth or Great Tree

units.leftText: They will greet you and give you two loaves of bread, which you will accept from their hands.
units.rightText: and they will salute thee, and give thee two loaves of bread, which thou shalt receive of their hand.

units.leftText: After that you will come to Gibeah of God, where the Philistines have an outpost. As you approach the city, you will meet a group of prophets coming down from the high place, preceded by harps, tambourines, flutes, and lyres, and they will be prophesying.
units.rightText: After that thou shalt come to the hill of God, where is the garrison of the Philistines: and it shall come to pass, when thou art come thither to the city, that thou shalt meet a band of prophets coming down from the high place with a psaltery, and a timbrel, and a pipe, and a harp, before them; and they will be prophesying:
leftNotes: 10:5 Hebrew Gibeath-Elohim, meaning the hill of God

units.leftText: Then the Spirit of the LORD will rush upon you, and you will prophesy with them; and you will be transformed into a different person.
units.rightText: and the Spirit of Jehovah will come mightily upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man.

units.leftText: When these signs have come, do as the occasion demands, for God is with you.
units.rightText: And let it be, when these signs are come unto thee, that thou do as occasion shall serve thee; for God is with thee.

units.leftText: And you shall go before me to Gilgal, and surely I will come to you to offer burnt offerings and to sacrifice peace offerings. Wait seven days until I come to you and show you what you are to do.” Samuel’s Signs Fulfilled
units.rightText: And thou shalt go down before me to Gilgal; and, behold, I will come down unto thee, to offer burnt-offerings, and to sacrifice sacrifices of peace-offerings: seven days shalt thou tarry, till I come unto thee, and show thee what thou shalt do.

units.leftText: As Saul turned to leave Samuel, God changed Saul’s heart, and all the signs came to pass that day.
units.rightText: And it was so, that, when he had turned his back to go from Samuel, God gave him another heart: and all those signs came to pass that day.

units.leftText: When Saul and his servant arrived at Gibeah, a group of prophets met him. Then the Spirit of God rushed upon him, and he prophesied along with them.
units.rightText: And when they came thither to the hill, behold, a band of prophets met him; and the Spirit of God came mightily upon him, and he prophesied among them.
leftNotes: 10:10 Gibeah means the hill.

units.leftText: When all those who had formerly known Saul saw him prophesying with the prophets, they asked one another, “What has happened to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when all that knew him beforetime saw that, behold, he prophesied with the prophets, then the people said one to another, What is this that is come unto the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?

units.leftText: Then a man who lived there replied, “And who is their father?” So the saying became a proverb: “Is Saul also among the prophets?”
units.rightText: And one of the same place answered and said, And who is their father? Therefore it became a proverb, Is Saul also among the prophets?

units.leftText: And when Saul had finished prophesying, he went up to the high place.
units.rightText: And when he had made an end of prophesying, he came to the high place.

units.leftText: Now Saul’s uncle asked him and his servant, “Where did you go?” “To look for the donkeys,” Saul replied. “When we saw they were not to be found, we went to Samuel.”
units.rightText: And Saul’s uncle said unto him and to his servant, Whither went ye? And he said, To seek the asses; and when we saw that they were not found, we came to Samuel.

units.leftText: “Tell me,” Saul’s uncle asked, “what did Samuel say to you?”
units.rightText: And Saul’s uncle said, Tell me, I pray thee, what Samuel said unto you.

units.leftText: And Saul replied, “He assured us that the donkeys had been found.” But Saul did not tell his uncle what Samuel had said about the kingship. Saul Proclaimed King
units.rightText: And Saul said unto his uncle, He told us plainly that the asses were found. But concerning the matter of the kingdom, whereof Samuel spake, he told him not.

units.leftText: After this, Samuel summoned the people to the LORD at Mizpah
units.rightText: And Samuel called the people together unto Jehovah to Mizpah;

units.leftText: and said to the Israelites, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘I brought Israel up out of Egypt, and I rescued you from the hands of the Egyptians and of all the kingdoms that oppressed you.’
units.rightText: and he said unto the children of Israel, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, I brought up Israel out of Egypt, and I delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of all the kingdoms that oppressed you:

units.leftText: But today you have rejected your God, who saves you from all your troubles and afflictions, and you have said to Him, ‘No, set a king over us.’ Now therefore present yourselves before the LORD by your tribes and clans.”
units.rightText: but ye have this day rejected your God, who himself saveth you out of all your calamities and your distresses; and ye have said unto him, Nay, but set a king over us. Now therefore present yourselves before Jehovah by your tribes, and by your thousands.

units.leftText: Thus Samuel had all the tribes of Israel come forward, and the tribe of Benjamin was selected.
units.rightText: So Samuel brought all the tribes of Israel near, and the tribe of Benjamin was taken.

units.leftText: Then he had the tribe of Benjamin come forward by its clans, and the clan of Matri was selected. Finally, Saul son of Kish was selected. But when they looked for him, they could not find him.
units.rightText: And he brought the tribe of Benjamin near by their families; and the family of the Matrites was taken; and Saul the son of Kish was taken: but when they sought him, he could not be found.
leftNotes: 10:21 LXX includes And he brought the family of the Matrites near, man by man.

units.leftText: So again they inquired of the LORD, “Has the man come here yet?” And the LORD replied, “Behold, he has hidden himself among the baggage.”
units.rightText: Therefore they asked of Jehovah further, Is there yet a man to come hither? And Jehovah answered, Behold, he hath hid himself among the baggage.
