units.leftText: So they ran and brought Saul, and when he stood among the people, he was a head taller than any of the others.
units.rightText: And they ran and fetched him thence; and when he stood among the people, he was higher than any of the people from his shoulders and upward.

units.leftText: Samuel said to all the people, “Do you see the one the LORD has chosen? There is no one like him among all the people.” And all the people shouted, “Long live the king!”
units.rightText: And Samuel said to all the people, See ye him whom Jehovah hath chosen, that there is none like him among all the people? And all the people shouted, and said, Long live the king.

units.leftText: Then Samuel explained to the people the rights of kingship. He wrote them on a scroll and laid it up before the LORD. And Samuel sent all the people away, each to his own home.
units.rightText: Then Samuel told the people the manner of the kingdom, and wrote it in a book, and laid it up before Jehovah. And Samuel sent all the people away, every man to his house.

units.leftText: Saul also went to his home in Gibeah, and the men of valor whose hearts God had touched went with him.
units.rightText: And Saul also went to his house to Gibeah; and there went with him the host, whose hearts God had touched.

units.leftText: But some worthless men said, “How can this man save us?” So they despised him and brought him no gifts; but Saul remained silent about it.
units.rightText: But certain worthless fellows said, How shall this man save us? And they despised him, and brought him no present. But he held his peace.
leftNotes: 10:27 MT and LXX; one DSS manuscript includes Nahash, king of the Ammonites, had viciously oppressed the people of Gad and Reuben, gouging out the right eye of each Israelite dwelling there. He would not allow anyone to rescue them, and there was no Israelite east of the Jordan whose right eye had not been gouged out. But 7,000 men had escaped from the Ammonites and settled in Jabesh-gilead.

units.leftText: Then Nahash the Ammonite came up and laid siege to Jabesh-gilead. All the men of Jabesh said to him, “Make a treaty with us, and we will serve you.”
units.rightText: Then Nahash the Ammonite came up, and encamped against Jabesh-gilead: and all the men of Jabesh said unto Nahash, Make a covenant with us, and we will serve thee.
leftNotes: 11:1 DSS and LXX About a month later Nahash
11:1 Forms of the Hebrew berit are translated in most passages as covenant.

units.leftText: But Nahash the Ammonite replied, “I will make a treaty with you on one condition, that I may put out everyone’s right eye and bring reproach upon all Israel.”
units.rightText: And Nahash the Ammonite said unto them, On this condition will I make it with you, that all your right eyes be put out; and I will lay it for a reproach upon all Israel.

units.leftText: “Hold off for seven days,” replied the elders of Jabesh, “and let us send messengers throughout Israel. If there is no one to save us, we will surrender to you.”
units.rightText: And the elders of Jabesh said unto him, Give us seven days’ respite, that we may send messengers unto all the borders of Israel; and then, if there be none to save us, we will come out to thee.

units.leftText: When the messengers came to Gibeah of Saul and relayed these words in the hearing of the people, they all wept aloud.
units.rightText: Then came the messengers to Gibeah of Saul, and spake these words in the ears of the people: and all the people lifted up their voice, and wept.

units.leftText: Just then Saul was returning from the field, behind his oxen. “What troubles the people?” asked Saul. “Why are they weeping?” And they relayed to him the words of the men from Jabesh.
units.rightText: And, behold, Saul came following the oxen out of the field; and Saul said, What aileth the people that they weep? And they told him the words of the men of Jabesh.

units.leftText: When Saul heard their words, the Spirit of God rushed upon him, and he burned with great anger.
units.rightText: And the Spirit of God came mightily upon Saul when he heard those words, and his anger was kindled greatly.

units.leftText: He took a pair of oxen, cut them into pieces, and sent them by messengers throughout the land of Israel, proclaiming, “This is what will be done to the oxen of anyone who does not march behind Saul and Samuel.”
units.rightText: And he took a yoke of oxen, and cut them in pieces, and sent them throughout all the borders of Israel by the hand of messengers, saying, Whosoever cometh not forth after Saul and after Samuel, so shall it be done unto his oxen. And the dread of Jehovah fell on the people, and they came out as one man.

units.leftText: And when Saul numbered them at Bezek, there were 300,000 Israelites and 30,000 men of Judah.
units.rightText: And he numbered them in Bezek; and the children of Israel were three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand.
leftNotes: 11:8 DSS and LXX 70,000

units.leftText: So they said to the messengers who had come, “Tell the men of Jabesh-gilead: ‘Deliverance will be yours tomorrow by the time the sun is hot.’” And when the messengers relayed this to the men of Jabesh, they rejoiced.
units.rightText: And they said unto the messengers that came, Thus shall ye say unto the men of Jabesh-gilead, To-morrow, by the time the sun is hot, ye shall have deliverance. And the messengers came and told the men of Jabesh; and they were glad.

units.leftText: Then the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, “Tomorrow we will come out, and you can do with us whatever seems good to you.”
units.rightText: Therefore the men of Jabesh said, To-morrow we will come out unto you, and ye shall do with us all that seemeth good unto you.

units.leftText: The next day Saul organized the troops into three divisions, and during the morning watch they invaded the camp of the Ammonites and slaughtered them, until the hottest part of the day. And the survivors were so scattered that no two of them were left together. Saul Confirmed as King
units.rightText: And it was so on the morrow, that Saul put the people in three companies; and they came into the midst of the camp in the morning watch, and smote the Ammonites until the heat of the day: and it came to pass, that they that remained were scattered, so that not two of them were left together.

units.leftText: Then the people said to Samuel, “Who said that Saul should not reign over us? Bring those men here so we can kill them!”
units.rightText: And the people said unto Samuel, Who is he that said, Shall Saul reign over us? bring the men, that we may put them to death.

units.leftText: But Saul ordered, “No one shall be put to death this day, for today the LORD has worked salvation in Israel.”
units.rightText: And Saul said, There shall not a man be put to death this day; for to-day Jehovah hath wrought deliverance in Israel.

units.leftText: Then Samuel said to the people, “Come, let us go to Gilgal and renew the kingship there.”
units.rightText: Then said Samuel to the people, Come, and let us go to Gilgal, and renew the kingdom there.

units.leftText: So all the people went to Gilgal and confirmed Saul as king in the presence of the LORD. There they sacrificed peace offerings before the LORD, and Saul and all the Israelites rejoiced greatly.
units.rightText: And all the people went to Gilgal; and there they made Saul king before Jehovah in Gilgal; and there they offered sacrifices of peace-offerings before Jehovah; and there Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced greatly.

units.leftText: Then Samuel said to all Israel, “I have listened to your voice in all that you have said to me, and I have set over you a king.
units.rightText: And Samuel said unto all Israel, Behold, I have hearkened unto your voice in all that ye said unto me, and have made a king over you.

units.leftText: Now here is the king walking before you, and I am old and gray, and my sons are here with you. I have walked before you from my youth until this day.
units.rightText: And now, behold, the king walketh before you; and I am old and grayheaded; and, behold, my sons are with you: and I have walked before you from my youth unto this day.

units.leftText: Here I am. Bear witness against me before the LORD and before His anointed: Whose ox or donkey have I taken? Whom have I cheated or oppressed? From whose hand have I accepted a bribe and closed my eyes? Tell me, and I will restore it to you.”
units.rightText: Here I am: witness against me before Jehovah, and before his anointed: whose ox have I taken? or whose ass have I taken? or whom have I defrauded? whom have I oppressed? or of whose hand have I taken a ransom to blind mine eyes therewith? and I will restore it you.
leftNotes: 12:3 Hebrew And I will restore it; LXX Testify against me, and I will restore it

units.leftText: “You have not cheated us or oppressed us,” they replied, “nor have you taken anything from the hand of man.”
units.rightText: And they said, Thou hast not defrauded us, nor oppressed us, neither hast thou taken aught of any man’s hand.

units.leftText: Samuel said to them, “The LORD is a witness against you, and His anointed is a witness today, that you have not found anything in my hand.” “He is a witness,” they replied.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Jehovah is witness against you, and his anointed is witness this day, that ye have not found aught in my hand. And they said, He is witness.

units.leftText: Then Samuel said to the people, “The LORD is the One who appointed Moses and Aaron, and who brought your fathers up out of the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: And Samuel said unto the people, It is Jehovah that appointed Moses and Aaron, and that brought your fathers up out of the land of Egypt.
leftNotes: 12:6 Hebrew; LXX The LORD is the witness who

units.leftText: Now present yourselves, so that I may confront you before the LORD with all the righteous acts He has done for you and your fathers.
units.rightText: Now therefore stand still, that I may plead with you before Jehovah concerning all the righteous acts of Jehovah, which he did to you and to your fathers.

units.leftText: When Jacob went to Egypt, your fathers cried out to the LORD, and He sent them Moses and Aaron, who brought your fathers out of Egypt and settled them in this place.
units.rightText: When Jacob was come into Egypt, and your fathers cried unto Jehovah, then Jehovah sent Moses and Aaron, who brought forth your fathers out of Egypt, and made them to dwell in this place.
leftNotes: 12:8 Hebrew; LXX includes and the Egyptians oppressed them

units.leftText: But they forgot the LORD their God, and He sold them into the hand of Sisera the commander of the army of Hazor, and into the hands of the Philistines and the king of Moab, who fought against them.
units.rightText: But they forgat Jehovah their God; and he sold them into the hand of Sisera, captain of the host of Hazor, and into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the king of Moab; and they fought against them.
leftNotes: 12:9 LXX the army of Jabin king of Hazor

units.leftText: Then they cried out to the LORD and said, ‘We have sinned, for we have forsaken the LORD and served the Baals and Ashtoreths. Now deliver us from the hands of our enemies, that we may serve You.’
units.rightText: And they cried unto Jehovah, and said, We have sinned, because we have forsaken Jehovah, and have served the Baalim and the Ashtaroth: but now deliver us out of the hand of our enemies, and we will serve thee.

units.leftText: So the LORD sent Jerubbaal, Barak, Jephthah, and Samuel, and He delivered you from the hands of your enemies on every side, and you dwelt securely.
units.rightText: And Jehovah sent Jerubbaal, and Bedan, and Jephthah, and Samuel, and delivered you out of the hand of your enemies on every side; and ye dwelt in safety.
leftNotes: 12:11 Jerubbaal is another name for Gideon and probably means let Baal contend; see Judges 6:32|JDG 6:32*.
12:11 LXX and Syriac; Hebrew Bedan
12:11 LXX and Syriac Samson

units.leftText: But when you saw that Nahash king of the Ammonites was moving against you, you said to me, ‘No, we must have a king to rule over us’— even though the LORD your God was your king.
units.rightText: And when ye saw that Nahash the king of the children of Ammon came against you, ye said unto me, Nay, but a king shall reign over us; when Jehovah your God was your king.

units.leftText: Now here is the king you have chosen, the one you requested. Behold, the LORD has placed a king over you.
units.rightText: Now therefore behold the king whom ye have chosen, and whom ye have asked for: and, behold, Jehovah hath set a king over you.

units.leftText: If you fear the LORD and serve Him and obey His voice, and if you do not rebel against the command of the LORD, and if both you and the king who rules over you follow the LORD your God, then all will be well.
units.rightText: If ye will fear Jehovah, and serve him, and hearken unto his voice, and not rebel against the commandment of Jehovah, and both ye and also the king that reigneth over you be followers of Jehovah your God, well:
leftNotes: 12:14 then all will be well is implied; Literally If you fear the LORD and serve Him and obey His voice, and if you do not rebel against the command of the LORD, (then) both you and the king who reigns over you will follow the LORD your God.

units.leftText: But if you disobey the LORD and rebel against His command, then the hand of the LORD will be against you as it was against your fathers.
units.rightText: but if ye will not hearken unto the voice of Jehovah, but rebel against the commandment of Jehovah, then will the hand of Jehovah be against you, as it was against your fathers.
leftNotes: 12:15 Hebrew; LXX against your king

units.leftText: Now, therefore, present yourselves and see this great thing that the LORD will do before your eyes.
units.rightText: Now therefore stand still and see this great thing, which Jehovah will do before your eyes.

units.leftText: Is it not the wheat harvest today? I will call on the LORD to send thunder and rain, so that you will know and see what a great evil you have committed in the sight of the LORD by asking for a king.”
units.rightText: Is it not wheat harvest to-day? I will call unto Jehovah, that he may send thunder and rain; and ye shall know and see that your wickedness is great, which ye have done in the sight of Jehovah, in asking you a king.

units.leftText: So Samuel called to the LORD, and on that day the LORD sent thunder and rain.
units.rightText: So Samuel called unto Jehovah; and Jehovah sent thunder and rain that day: and all the people greatly feared Jehovah and Samuel.

units.leftText: They pleaded with Samuel, “Pray to the LORD your God for your servants so that we will not die! For we have added to all our sins the evil of asking for a king.”
units.rightText: And all the people said unto Samuel, Pray for thy servants unto Jehovah thy God, that we die not; for we have added unto all our sins this evil, to ask us a king.

units.leftText: “Do not be afraid,” Samuel replied. “Even though you have committed all this evil, do not turn aside from following the LORD, but serve the LORD with all your heart.
units.rightText: And Samuel said unto the people, Fear not: ye have indeed done all this evil; yet turn not aside from following Jehovah, but serve Jehovah with all your heart:

units.leftText: Do not turn aside after worthless things that cannot profit you or deliver you, for they are empty.
units.rightText: and turn ye not aside; for then would ye go after vain things which cannot profit nor deliver, for they are vain.

units.leftText: Indeed, for the sake of His great name, the LORD will not abandon His people, because He was pleased to make you His own.
units.rightText: For Jehovah will not forsake his people for his great name’s sake, because it hath pleased Jehovah to make you a people unto himself.

units.leftText: As for me, far be it from me that I should sin against the LORD by ceasing to pray for you. And I will continue to teach you the good and right way.
units.rightText: Moreover as for me, far be it from me that I should sin against Jehovah in ceasing to pray for you: but I will instruct you in the good and the right way.

units.leftText: Above all, fear the LORD and serve Him faithfully with all your heart; consider what great things He has done for you.
units.rightText: Only fear Jehovah, and serve him in truth with all your heart; for consider how great things he hath done for you.

units.leftText: But if you persist in doing evil, both you and your king will be swept away.”
units.rightText: But if ye shall still do wickedly, ye shall be consumed, both ye and your king.

units.leftText: Saul was thirty years old when he became king, and he reigned over Israel forty-two years.
units.rightText: Saul was forty years old when he began to reign; and when he had reigned two years over Israel,
leftNotes: 13:1 A few late LXX manuscripts; MT Saul was a son of a year
13:1 Or over Israel forty years(see Acts 13:21|ACT 13:21*); MT over Israel two years

units.leftText: He chose for himself three thousand men of Israel: Two thousand were with Saul at Michmash and in the hill country of Bethel, and a thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin. And the rest of the troops he sent away, each to his own home.
units.rightText: Saul chose him three thousand men of Israel, whereof two thousand were with Saul in Michmash and in the mount of Beth-el, and a thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin: and the rest of the people he sent every man to his tent.

units.leftText: Then Jonathan attacked the Philistine outpost at Geba, and the Philistines heard about it. So Saul blew the ram’s horn throughout the land, saying, “Let the Hebrews hear!”
units.rightText: And Jonathan smote the garrison of the Philistines that was in Geba; and the Philistines heard of it. And Saul blew the trumpet throughout all the land, saying, Let the Hebrews hear.

units.leftText: And all Israel heard the news: “Saul has attacked an outpost of the Philistines, and now Israel has become a stench to the Philistines!” Then the people were summoned to join Saul at Gilgal.
units.rightText: And all Israel heard say that Saul had smitten the garrison of the Philistines, and also that Israel was had in abomination with the Philistines. And the people were gathered together after Saul to Gilgal.

units.leftText: Now the Philistines assembled to fight against Israel with three thousand chariots, six thousand horsemen, and troops as numerous as the sand on the seashore. They went up and camped at Michmash, east of Beth-aven.
units.rightText: And the Philistines assembled themselves together to fight with Israel, thirty thousand chariots, and six thousand horsemen, and people as the sand which is on the sea-shore in multitude: and they came up, and encamped in Michmash, eastward of Beth-aven.
leftNotes: 13:5 Some LXX manuscripts and Syriac; Hebrew thirty thousand

units.leftText: Seeing that they were in danger because their troops were hard-pressed, the men of Israel hid in caves and thickets, among the rocks, and in cellars and cisterns.
units.rightText: When the men of Israel saw that they were in a strait (for the people were distressed), then the people did hide themselves in caves, and in thickets, and in rocks, and in coverts, and in pits.

units.leftText: Some Hebrews even crossed the Jordan into the land of Gad and Gilead. Saul, however, remained at Gilgal, and all his troops were quaking in fear. Saul’s Unlawful Sacrifice
units.rightText: Now some of the Hebrews had gone over the Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead; but as for Saul, he was yet in Gilgal, and all the people followed him trembling.

units.leftText: And Saul waited seven days for the time appointed by Samuel, but Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and the troops began to desert Saul.
units.rightText: And he tarried seven days, according to the set time that Samuel had appointed: but Samuel came not to Gilgal; and the people were scattered from him.

units.leftText: So he said, “Bring me the burnt offering and the peace offerings.” And he offered up the burnt offering.
units.rightText: And Saul said, Bring hither the burnt-offering to me, and the peace-offerings. And he offered the burnt-offering.

units.leftText: Just as he finished offering the burnt offering, Samuel arrived, and Saul went out to greet him.
units.rightText: And it came to pass that, as soon as he had made an end of offering the burnt-offering, behold, Samuel came; and Saul went out to meet him, that he might salute him.

units.leftText: “What have you done?” Samuel asked.
units.rightText: And Samuel said, What hast thou done? And Saul said, Because I saw that the people were scattered from me, and that thou camest not within the days appointed, and that the Philistines assembled themselves together at Michmash;

units.leftText: I thought, ‘Now the Philistines will descend upon me at Gilgal, and I have not sought the favor of the LORD.’ So I felt compelled to offer the burnt offering.”
units.rightText: therefore said I, Now will the Philistines come down upon me to Gilgal, and I have not entreated the favor of Jehovah: I forced myself therefore, and offered the burnt-offering.

units.leftText: “You have acted foolishly,” Samuel declared. “You have not kept the command that the LORD your God gave you; if you had, the LORD would have established your kingdom over Israel for all time.
units.rightText: And Samuel said to Saul, Thou hast done foolishly; thou hast not kept the commandment of Jehovah thy God, which he commanded thee: for now would Jehovah have established thy kingdom upon Israel for ever.

units.leftText: But now your kingdom will not endure; the LORD has sought a man after His own heart and appointed him ruler over His people, because you have not kept the command of the LORD.”
units.rightText: But now thy kingdom shall not continue: Jehovah hath sought him a man after his own heart, and Jehovah hath appointed him to be prince over his people, because thou hast not kept that which Jehovah commanded thee.

units.leftText: Then Samuel set out from Gilgal and went up to Gibeah in Benjamin. And Saul numbered the troops who were with him, about six hundred men. Israel without Weapons
units.rightText: And Samuel arose, and gat him up from Gilgal unto Gibeah of Benjamin. And Saul numbered the people that were present with him, about six hundred men.
leftNotes: 13:15 LXX Then Samuel set out, and the rest of the people went up after Saul to meet the army; they went up from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin.

units.leftText: Now Saul and Jonathan his son and the troops with them were staying in Geba of Benjamin, while the Philistines camped at Michmash.
units.rightText: And Saul, and Jonathan his son, and the people that were present with them, abode in Geba of Benjamin: but the Philistines encamped in Michmash.

units.leftText: And raiders went out of the Philistine camp in three divisions. One headed toward Ophrah in the land of Shual,
units.rightText: And the spoilers came out of the camp of the Philistines in three companies: one company turned unto the way that leadeth to Ophrah, unto the land of Shual;

units.leftText: another toward Beth-horon, and the third down the border road overlooking the Valley of Zeboim facing the wilderness.
units.rightText: and another company turned the way to Beth-horon; and another company turned the way of the border that looketh down upon the valley of Zeboim toward the wilderness.

units.leftText: And no blacksmith could be found in all the land of Israel, because the Philistines had said, “The Hebrews must not be allowed to make swords or spears.”
units.rightText: Now there was no smith found throughout all the land of Israel; for the Philistines said, Lest the Hebrews make them swords or spears:

units.leftText: Instead, all the Israelites would go down to the Philistines to sharpen their plowshares, mattocks, axes, and sickles.
units.rightText: but all the Israelites went down to the Philistines, to sharpen every man his share, and his coulter, and his axe, and his mattock;
leftNotes: 13:20 LXX; Hebrew and plowshares; (so plowshare appears twice in the Hebrew).

units.leftText: The charge was a pim for sharpening a plowshare or mattock, a third of a shekel for sharpening a pitchfork or an axe, and a third of a shekel for repointing an oxgoad.
units.rightText: yet they had a file for the mattocks, and for the coulters, and for the forks, and for the axes, and to set the goads.
leftNotes: 13:21 A pim possibly refers to a polished stone weighing approximately 0.25 ounces or 7 grams found in excavations. This is equivalent to about two-thirds of a shekel and likely refers to the price charged by the Philistines for the services listed.
13:21 Hebrew does not include the currency unit of a shekel charged for sharpening a pitchfork, an axe, or an oxgoad; alternatively, possibly a third of a pim for each.

units.leftText: So on the day of battle not a sword or spear could be found in the hands of the troops with Saul and Jonathan; only Saul and his son Jonathan had weapons.
units.rightText: So it came to pass in the day of battle, that there was neither sword nor spear found in the hand of any of the people that were with Saul and Jonathan: but with Saul and with Jonathan his son was there found.

units.leftText: And a garrison of the Philistines had gone out to the pass at Michmash.
units.rightText: And the garrison of the Philistines went out unto the pass of Michmash.

units.leftText: One day Jonathan son of Saul said to the young man bearing his armor, “Come, let us cross over to the Philistine outpost on the other side.” But Jonathan did not tell his father.
units.rightText: Now it fell upon a day, that Jonathan the son of Saul said unto the young man that bare his armor, Come, and let us go over to the Philistines’ garrison, that is on yonder side. But he told not his father.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, Saul was staying under the pomegranate tree in Migron on the outskirts of Gibeah. And the troops who were with him numbered about six hundred men,
units.rightText: And Saul abode in the uttermost part of Gibeah under the pomegranate-tree which is in Migron: and the people that were with him were about six hundred men;
leftNotes: 14:2 Or around the rock of Rimmon or in the pomegranate cave; see Judges 20:45|JDG 20:45*, Judges 20:47, and Judges 21:13.

units.leftText: including Ahijah, who was wearing an ephod. He was the son of Ichabod’s brother Ahitub son of Phinehas, the son of Eli the priest of the LORD in Shiloh. But the troops did not know that Jonathan had left.
units.rightText: and Ahijah, the son of Ahitub, Ichabod’s brother, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eli, the priest of Jehovah in Shiloh, wearing an ephod. And the people knew not that Jonathan was gone.

units.leftText: Now there were cliffs on both sides of the pass that Jonathan intended to cross to reach the Philistine outpost. One was named Bozez and the other Seneh.
units.rightText: And between the passes, by which Jonathan sought to go over unto the Philistines’ garrison, there was a rocky crag on the one side, and a rocky crag on the other side: and the name of the one was Bozez, and the name of the other Seneh.

units.leftText: One cliff stood to the north toward Michmash, and the other to the south toward Geba.
units.rightText: The one crag rose up on the north in front of Michmash, and the other on the south in front of Geba.

units.leftText: Jonathan said to the young man bearing his armor, “Come, let us cross over to the outpost of these uncircumcised men. Perhaps the LORD will work on our behalf. Nothing can hinder the LORD from saving, whether by many or by few.”
units.rightText: And Jonathan said to the young man that bare his armor, Come, and let us go over unto the garrison of these uncircumcised: it may be that Jehovah will work for us; for there is no restraint to Jehovah to save by many or by few.

units.leftText: His armor-bearer replied, “Do all that is in your heart. Go ahead; I am with you heart and soul.”
units.rightText: And his armorbearer said unto him, Do all that is in thy heart: turn thee, behold, I am with thee according to thy heart.

units.leftText: “Very well,” said Jonathan, “we will cross over toward these men and show ourselves to them.
units.rightText: Then said Jonathan, Behold, we will pass over unto the men, and we will disclose ourselves unto them.

units.leftText: If they say, ‘Wait until we come to you,’ then we will stay where we are and will not go up to them.
units.rightText: If they say thus unto us, Tarry until we come to you; then we will stand still in our place, and will not go up unto them.

units.leftText: But if they say, ‘Come on up,’ then we will go up, because this will be our sign that the LORD has delivered them into our hands.”
units.rightText: But if they say thus, Come up unto us; then we will go up; for Jehovah hath delivered them into our hand: and this shall be the sign unto us.

units.leftText: So the two of them showed themselves to the outpost of the Philistines, who exclaimed, “Look, the Hebrews are coming out of the holes in which they were hiding!”
units.rightText: And both of them disclosed themselves unto the garrison of the Philistines: and the Philistines said, Behold, the Hebrews come forth out of the holes where they had hid themselves.

units.leftText: So the men of the outpost called out to Jonathan and his armor-bearer, “Come on up, and we will teach you a lesson!” “Follow me,” Jonathan told his armor-bearer, “for the LORD has delivered them into the hand of Israel.”
units.rightText: And the men of the garrison answered Jonathan and his armorbearer, and said, Come up to us, and we will show you a thing. And Jonathan said unto his armorbearer, Come up after me; for Jehovah hath delivered them into the hand of Israel.

units.leftText: So Jonathan climbed up on his hands and feet, with his armor-bearer behind him. And the Philistines fell before Jonathan, and his armor-bearer followed and finished them off.
units.rightText: And Jonathan climbed up upon his hands and upon his feet, and his armorbearer after him: and they fell before Jonathan; and his armorbearer slew them after him.

units.leftText: In that first assault, Jonathan and his armor-bearer struck down about twenty men in about half an acre of land.
units.rightText: And that first slaughter, which Jonathan and his armorbearer made, was about twenty men, within as it were half a furrow’s length in an acre of land.
leftNotes: 14:14 Hebrew half a yoke. A yoke was the amount of land plowed by a pair of yoked oxen in one day.

units.leftText: Then panic struck the Philistines in the camp, in the field, and among all the people. Even those in the outposts and raiding parties trembled. Indeed, the earth quaked, and panic spread from God.
units.rightText: And there was a trembling in the camp, in the field, and among all the people; the garrison, and the spoilers, they also trembled; and the earth quaked: so there was an exceeding great trembling.
leftNotes: 14:15 Or and a terrible panic spread

units.leftText: Now when Saul’s watchmen at Gibeah in Benjamin looked and saw the troops melting away and scattering in every direction,
units.rightText: And the watchmen of Saul in Gibeah of Benjamin looked; and, behold, the multitude melted away, and they went hither and thither.
leftNotes: 14:16 Or melting away and going here and there

units.leftText: Saul said to the troops who were with him, “Call the roll and see who has left us.” And when they had called the roll, they saw that Jonathan and his armor-bearer were not there.
units.rightText: Then said Saul unto the people that were with him, Number now, and see who is gone from us. And when they had numbered, behold, Jonathan and his armorbearer were not there.

units.leftText: Then Saul said to Ahijah, “Bring the ark of God.” (For at that time it was with the Israelites.)
units.rightText: And Saul said unto Ahijah, Bring hither the ark of God. For the ark of God was there at that time with the children of Israel.
leftNotes: 14:18 Hebrew; LXX “Bring the ephod.” For at that time he wore the ephod before the Israelites.

units.leftText: While Saul was talking to the priest, the commotion in the Philistine camp continued to increase. So Saul said to the priest, “Withdraw your hand.”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, while Saul talked unto the priest, that the tumult that was in the camp of the Philistines went on and increased: and Saul said unto the priest, Withdraw thy hand.

units.leftText: Then Saul and all his troops assembled and marched to the battle, and they found the Philistines in total confusion, with each man wielding the sword against his neighbor.
units.rightText: And Saul and all the people that were with him were gathered together, and came to the battle: and, behold, every man’s sword was against his fellow, and there was a very great discomfiture.

units.leftText: And the Hebrews who had previously gone up into the surrounding camps to join the Philistines now went over to the Israelites who were with Saul and Jonathan.
units.rightText: Now the Hebrews that were with the Philistines as beforetime, and that went up with them into the camp, from the country round about, even they also turned to be with the Israelites that were with Saul and Jonathan.

units.leftText: When all the Israelites who had been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim heard that the Philistines were fleeing, they also joined the battle in close pursuit.
units.rightText: Likewise all the men of Israel that had hid themselves in the hill-country of Ephraim, when they heard that the Philistines fled, even they also followed hard after them in the battle.

units.leftText: So the LORD saved Israel that day, and the battle moved on beyond Beth-aven. Jonathan Eats the Honey
units.rightText: So Jehovah saved Israel that day: and the battle passed over by Beth-aven.

units.leftText: Now the men of Israel were in distress that day, for Saul had placed the troops under an oath, saying, “Cursed is the man who eats any food before evening, before I have taken vengeance on my enemies.” So none of the troops tasted any food.
units.rightText: And the men of Israel were distressed that day; for Saul had adjured the people, saying, Cursed be the man that eateth any food until it be evening, and I be avenged on mine enemies. So none of the people tasted food.

units.leftText: Then all the troops entered the forest, and there was honey on the ground.
units.rightText: And all the people came into the forest; and there was honey upon the ground.

units.leftText: And when they entered the forest and saw the flowing honey, not one of them put his hand to his mouth, because they feared the oath.
units.rightText: And when the people were come unto the forest, behold, the honey dropped: but no man put his hand to his mouth; for the people feared the oath.

units.leftText: Jonathan, however, had not heard that his father had bound the people with the oath. So he reached out the end of the staff in his hand, dipped it into the honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth, and his eyes brightened.
units.rightText: But Jonathan heard not when his father charged the people with the oath: wherefore he put forth the end of the rod that was in his hand, and dipped it in the honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth; and his eyes were enlightened.
leftNotes: 14:27 Or his strength was renewed; similarly in verse 29

units.leftText: Then one of the soldiers told him, “Your father bound the troops with a solemn oath, saying, ‘Cursed is the man who eats food today.’ That is why the people are faint.”
units.rightText: Then answered one of the people, and said, Thy father straitly charged the people with an oath, saying, Cursed be the man that eateth food this day. And the people were faint.

units.leftText: “My father has brought trouble to the land,” Jonathan replied. “Just look at how my eyes have brightened because I tasted a little of this honey.
units.rightText: Then said Jonathan, My father hath troubled the land: see, I pray you, how mine eyes have been enlightened, because I tasted a little of this honey.

units.leftText: How much better it would have been if the troops had eaten freely today from the plunder they took from their enemies! Would not the slaughter of the Philistines have been much greater?”
units.rightText: How much more, if haply the people had eaten freely to-day of the spoil of their enemies which they found? for now hath there been no great slaughter among the Philistines.

units.leftText: That day, after the Israelites had struck down the Philistines from Michmash to Aijalon, the people were very faint.
units.rightText: And they smote of the Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon. And the people were very faint;

units.leftText: So they rushed greedily to the plunder, taking sheep, cattle, and calves. They slaughtered them on the ground and ate meat with the blood still in it.
units.rightText: and the people flew upon the spoil, and took sheep, and oxen, and calves, and slew them on the ground; and the people did eat them with the blood.

units.leftText: Then someone reported to Saul: “Look, the troops are sinning against the LORD by eating meat with the blood still in it.”
units.rightText: Then they told Saul, saying, Behold, the people sin against Jehovah, in that they eat with the blood. And he said, Ye have dealt treacherously: roll a great stone unto me this day.

units.leftText: Then he said, “Go among the troops and tell them, ‘Each man must bring me his ox or his sheep, slaughter them in this place, and then eat. Do not sin against the LORD by eating meat with the blood still in it.’”
units.rightText: And Saul said, Disperse yourselves among the people, and say unto them, Bring me hither every man his ox, and every man his sheep, and slay them here, and eat; and sin not against Jehovah in eating with the blood. And all the people brought every man his ox with him that night, and slew them there.

units.leftText: Then Saul built an altar to the LORD; it was the first time he had built an altar to the LORD.
units.rightText: And Saul built an altar unto Jehovah: the same was the first altar that he built unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: And Saul said, “Let us go down after the Philistines by night and plunder them until dawn, leaving no man alive!” “Do what seems good to you,” the troops replied. But the priest said, “We must consult God here.” The People Save Jonathan
units.rightText: And Saul said, Let us go down after the Philistines by night, and take spoil among them until the morning light, and let us not leave a man of them. And they said, Do whatsoever seemeth good unto thee. Then said the priest, Let us draw near hither unto God.

units.leftText: So Saul inquired of God, “Shall I go down after the Philistines? Will You give them into the hand of Israel?” But God did not answer him that day.
units.rightText: And Saul asked counsel of God, Shall I go down after the Philistines? wilt thou deliver them into the hand of Israel? But he answered him not that day.

units.leftText: Therefore Saul said, “Come here, all you leaders of the troops, and let us investigate how this sin has occurred today.
units.rightText: And Saul said, Draw nigh hither, all ye chiefs of the people; and know and see wherein this sin hath been this day.

units.leftText: As surely as the LORD who saves Israel lives, even if it is my son Jonathan, he must die!” But not one of the troops said a word.
units.rightText: For, as Jehovah liveth, who saveth Israel, though it be in Jonathan my son, he shall surely die. But there was not a man among all the people that answered him.

units.leftText: Then Saul said to all Israel, “You stand on one side, and I and my son Jonathan will stand on the other side.” “Do what seems good to you,” the troops replied.
units.rightText: Then said he unto all Israel, Be ye on one side, and I and Jonathan my son will be on the other side. And the people said unto Saul, Do what seemeth good unto thee.

units.leftText: So Saul said to the LORD, the God of Israel, “Why have You not answered Your servant this day? If the fault is with me or my son Jonathan, respond with Urim, but if the fault is with the men of Israel, respond with Thummim.” And Jonathan and Saul were selected, but the people were cleared of the charge.
units.rightText: Therefore Saul said unto Jehovah, the God of Israel, Show the right. And Jonathan and Saul were taken by lot; but the people escaped.
leftNotes: 14:41 LXX and Vulgate; MT contains only the short quotation, “Give a perfect (lot).”

units.leftText: Then Saul said, “Cast the lot between me and my son Jonathan.” And Jonathan was selected.
units.rightText: And Saul said, Cast lots between me and Jonathan my son. And Jonathan was taken.

units.leftText: “Tell me what you have done,” Saul commanded him. So Jonathan told him, “I only tasted a little honey with the end of the staff that was in my hand. And now I must die?”
units.rightText: Then Saul said to Jonathan, Tell me what thou hast done. And Jonathan told him, and said, I did certainly taste a little honey with the end of the rod that was in my hand; and, lo, I must die.

units.leftText: And Saul declared, “May God punish me, and ever so severely, if you, Jonathan, do not surely die!”
units.rightText: And Saul said, God do so and more also; for thou shalt surely die, Jonathan.

units.leftText: But the people said to Saul, “Must Jonathan die — he who accomplished such a great deliverance for Israel? Never! As surely as the LORD lives, not a hair of his head will fall to the ground, for with God’s help he has accomplished this today.”
units.rightText: And the people said unto Saul, Shall Jonathan die, who hath wrought this great salvation in Israel? Far from it: as Jehovah liveth, there shall not one hair of his head fall to the ground; for he hath wrought with God this day. So the people rescued Jonathan, that he died not.

units.leftText: Then Saul gave up his pursuit of the Philistines, and the Philistines returned to their own land. Saul’s Victories
units.rightText: Then Saul went up from following the Philistines; and the Philistines went to their own place.

units.leftText: After Saul had assumed the kingship over Israel, he fought against all his enemies on every side — the Moabites, the Ammonites, the Edomites, the kings of Zobah, and the Philistines. Wherever he turned, he routed them.
units.rightText: Now when Saul had taken the kingdom over Israel, he fought against all his enemies on every side, against Moab, and against the children of Ammon, and against Edom, and against the kings of Zobah, and against the Philistines: and whithersoever he turned himself, he put them to the worse.
leftNotes: 14:47 MT; DSS and LXX king
14:47 Or he inflicted punishment on them from Hebrew; LXX he was victorious

units.leftText: He fought valiantly and defeated the Amalekites, delivering Israel from the hands of its plunderers.
units.rightText: And he did valiantly, and smote the Amalekites, and delivered Israel out of the hands of them that despoiled them.

units.leftText: Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchishua. His two daughters were named Merab (his firstborn) and Michal (his younger daughter).
units.rightText: Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, and Ishvi, and Malchishua; and the names of his two daughters were these: the name of the first-born Merab, and the name of the younger Michal:

units.leftText: His wife’s name was Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz. The name of the commander of his army was Abner, the son of Saul’s uncle Ner.
units.rightText: and the name of Saul’s wife was Ahinoam the daughter of Ahimaaz. And the name of the captain of his host was Abner the son of Ner, Saul’s uncle.

units.leftText: Saul’s father Kish and Abner’s father Ner were sons of Abiel.
units.rightText: And Kish was the father of Saul; and Ner the father of Abner was the son of Abiel.

units.leftText: And the war with the Philistines was fierce for all the days of Saul. So whenever he noticed any strong or brave man, Saul would enlist him.
units.rightText: And there was sore war against the Philistines all the days of Saul: and when Saul saw any mighty man, or any valiant man, he took him unto him.

units.leftText: Then Samuel said to Saul, “The LORD sent me to anoint you king over His people Israel. Now therefore, listen to the words of the LORD.
units.rightText: And Samuel said unto Saul, Jehovah sent me to anoint thee to be king over his people, over Israel: now therefore hearken thou unto the voice of the words of Jehovah.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: ‘I witnessed what the Amalekites did to the Israelites when they opposed them on their way up from Egypt.
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah of hosts, I have marked that which Amalek did to Israel, how he set himself against him in the way, when he came up out of Egypt.

units.leftText: Now go and attack the Amalekites and devote to destruction all that belongs to them. Do not spare them, but put to death men and women, children and infants, oxen and sheep, camels and donkeys.’”
units.rightText: Now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not; but slay both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass.
leftNotes: 15:3 Forms of the Hebrew cherem refer to the giving over of things or persons to the LORD, either by destroying them or by giving them as an offering; also in verses 8, 9, 15, 18, 20, and 21.

units.leftText: So Saul summoned the troops and numbered them at Telaim — 200,000 foot soldiers and 10,000 men of Judah.
units.rightText: And Saul summoned the people, and numbered them in Telaim, two hundred thousand footmen, and ten thousand men of Judah.

units.leftText: Saul came to the city of Amalek and lay in wait in the valley.
units.rightText: And Saul came to the city of Amalek, and laid wait in the valley.

units.leftText: And he warned the Kenites, “Since you showed kindness to all the Israelites when they came up out of Egypt, go on and get away from the Amalekites. Otherwise I will sweep you away with them.” So the Kenites moved away from the Amalekites.
units.rightText: And Saul said unto the Kenites, Go, depart, get you down from among the Amalekites, lest I destroy you with them; for ye showed kindness to all the children of Israel, when they came up out of Egypt. So the Kenites departed from among the Amalekites.

units.leftText: Then Saul struck down the Amalekites all the way from Havilah to Shur, which is east of Egypt.
units.rightText: And Saul smote the Amalekites, from Havilah as thou goest to Shur, that is before Egypt.

units.leftText: He captured Agag king of Amalek alive, but devoted all the others to destruction with the sword.
units.rightText: And he took Agag the king of the Amalekites alive, and utterly destroyed all the people with the edge of the sword.

units.leftText: Saul and his troops spared Agag, along with the best of the sheep and cattle, the fat calves and lambs, and the best of everything else. They were unwilling to devote them to destruction, but they devoted to destruction all that was despised and worthless. Samuel Denounces Saul
units.rightText: But Saul and the people spared Agag, and the best of the sheep, and of the oxen, and of the fatlings, and the lambs, and all that was good, and would not utterly destroy them: but everything that was vile and refuse, that they destroyed utterly.
leftNotes: 15:9 Or the grown bulls

units.leftText: Then the word of the LORD came to Samuel, saying,
units.rightText: Then came the word of Jehovah unto Samuel, saying,

units.leftText: “I regret that I have made Saul king, for he has turned away from following Me and has not carried out My instructions.” And Samuel was distressed and cried out to the LORD all that night.
units.rightText: It repenteth me that I have set up Saul to be king; for he is turned back from following me, and hath not performed my commandments. And Samuel was wroth; and he cried unto Jehovah all night.

units.leftText: Early in the morning Samuel got up to confront Saul, but he was told, “Saul has gone to Carmel, and behold, he has set up a monument for himself and has turned and gone down to Gilgal.”
units.rightText: And Samuel rose early to meet Saul in the morning; and it was told Samuel, saying, Saul came to Carmel, and, behold, he set him up a monument, and turned, and passed on, and went down to Gilgal.

units.leftText: When Samuel reached him, Saul said to him, “May the LORD bless you. I have carried out the LORD’s instructions.”
units.rightText: And Samuel came to Saul; and Saul said unto him, Blessed be thou of Jehovah: I have performed the commandment of Jehovah.

units.leftText: But Samuel replied, “Then what is this bleating of sheep and lowing of cattle that I hear?”
units.rightText: And Samuel said, What meaneth then this bleating of the sheep in mine ears, and the lowing of the oxen which I hear?

units.leftText: Saul answered, “The troops brought them from the Amalekites; they spared the best sheep and cattle to sacrifice to the LORD your God, but the rest we devoted to destruction.”
units.rightText: And Saul said, They have brought them from the Amalekites: for the people spared the best of the sheep and of the oxen, to sacrifice unto Jehovah thy God; and the rest we have utterly destroyed.

units.leftText: “Stop!” exclaimed Samuel. “Let me tell you what the LORD said to me last night.” “Tell me,” Saul replied.
units.rightText: Then Samuel said unto Saul, Stay, and I will tell thee what Jehovah hath said to me this night. And he said unto him, Say on.

units.leftText: And Samuel said, “Although you were once small in your own eyes, have you not become the head of the tribes of Israel? The LORD anointed you king over Israel
units.rightText: And Samuel said, Though thou wast little in thine own sight, wast thou not made the head of the tribes of Israel? And Jehovah anointed thee king over Israel;

units.leftText: and sent you on a mission, saying, ‘Go and devote to destruction the sinful Amalekites. Fight against them until you have wiped them out.’
units.rightText: and Jehovah sent thee on a journey, and said, Go, and utterly destroy the sinners the Amalekites, and fight against them until they be consumed.

units.leftText: So why did you not obey the LORD? Why did you rush upon the plunder and do evil in the sight of the LORD?”
units.rightText: Wherefore then didst thou not obey the voice of Jehovah, but didst fly upon the spoil, and didst that which was evil in the sight of Jehovah?

units.leftText: “But I did obey the LORD,” Saul replied. “I went on the mission that the LORD gave me. I brought back Agag king of Amalek and devoted the Amalekites to destruction.
units.rightText: And Saul said unto Samuel, Yea, I have obeyed the voice of Jehovah, and have gone the way which Jehovah sent me, and have brought Agag the king of Amalek, and have utterly destroyed the Amalekites.

units.leftText: The troops took sheep and cattle from the plunder, the best of the things devoted to destruction, in order to sacrifice them to the LORD your God at Gilgal.”
units.rightText: But the people took of the spoil, sheep and oxen, the chief of the devoted things, to sacrifice unto Jehovah thy God in Gilgal.

units.leftText: But Samuel declared: “Does the LORD delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as much as in obedience to His voice? Behold, obedience is better than sacrifice, and attentiveness is better than the fat of rams.
units.rightText: And Samuel said, Hath Jehovah as great delight in burnt-offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of Jehovah? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.

units.leftText: For rebellion is like the sin of divination, and arrogance is like the wickedness of idolatry. Because you have rejected the word of the LORD, He has rejected you as king.” Saul’s Confession
units.rightText: For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as idolatry and teraphim. Because thou hast rejected the word of Jehovah, he hath also rejected thee from being king.

units.leftText: Then Saul said to Samuel, “I have sinned; I have transgressed the LORD’s commandment and your instructions, because I feared the people and obeyed their voice.
units.rightText: And Saul said unto Samuel, I have sinned; for I have transgressed the commandment of Jehovah, and thy words, because I feared the people, and obeyed their voice.

units.leftText: Now therefore, please forgive my sin and return with me so I can worship the LORD.”
units.rightText: Now therefore, I pray thee, pardon my sin, and turn again with me, that I may worship Jehovah.

units.leftText: “I will not return with you,” Samuel replied. “For you have rejected the word of the LORD, and He has rejected you as king over Israel.”
units.rightText: And Samuel said unto Saul, I will not return with thee; for thou hast rejected the word of Jehovah, and Jehovah hath rejected thee from being king over Israel.

units.leftText: As Samuel turned to go, Saul grabbed the hem of his robe, and it tore.
units.rightText: And as Samuel turned about to go away, Saul laid hold upon the skirt of his robe, and it rent.

units.leftText: So Samuel said to him, “The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today and has given it to your neighbor who is better than you.
units.rightText: And Samuel said unto him, Jehovah hath rent the kingdom of Israel from thee this day, and hath given it to a neighbor of thine, that is better than thou.

units.leftText: Moreover, the Glory of Israel does not lie or change His mind, for He is not a man, that He should change His mind.”
units.rightText: And also the Strength of Israel will not lie nor repent; for he is not a man, that he should repent.

units.leftText: “I have sinned,” Saul replied. “Please honor me now before the elders of my people and before Israel. Come back with me, so that I may worship the LORD your God.”
units.rightText: Then he said, I have sinned: yet honor me now, I pray thee, before the elders of my people, and before Israel, and turn again with me, that I may worship Jehovah thy God.

units.leftText: So Samuel went back with Saul, and Saul worshiped the LORD.
units.rightText: So Samuel turned again after Saul; and Saul worshipped Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then Samuel said, “Bring me Agag king of the Amalekites.” Agag came to him cheerfully, for he thought, “Surely the bitterness of death is past.”
units.rightText: Then said Samuel, Bring ye hither to me Agag the king of the Amalekites. And Agag came unto him cheerfully. And Agag said, Surely the bitterness of death is past.
leftNotes: 15:32 Or cautiously or in chains; see DSS and LXX.
15:32 Or “Surely this is the bitterness of death.” See DSS and LXX.

units.leftText: But Samuel declared: “As your sword has made women childless, so your mother will be childless among women.” And Samuel hacked Agag to pieces before the LORD at Gilgal.
units.rightText: And Samuel said, As thy sword hath made women childless, so shall thy mother be childless among women. And Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before Jehovah in Gilgal.

units.leftText: Then Samuel went to Ramah, but Saul went up to his home in Gibeah of Saul.
units.rightText: Then Samuel went to Ramah; and Saul went up to his house to Gibeah of Saul.

units.leftText: And to the day of his death, Samuel never again visited Saul. Samuel mourned for Saul, and the LORD regretted that He had made Saul king over Israel.
units.rightText: And Samuel came no more to see Saul until the day of his death; for Samuel mourned for Saul: and Jehovah repented that he had made Saul king over Israel.

units.leftText: Now the LORD said to Samuel, “How long are you going to mourn for Saul, since I have rejected him as king over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and go. I am sending you to Jesse of Bethlehem, for I have selected from his sons a king for Myself.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Samuel, How long wilt thou mourn for Saul, seeing I have rejected him from being king over Israel? fill thy horn with oil, and go: I will send thee to Jesse the Beth-lehemite; for I have provided me a king among his sons.

units.leftText: “How can I go?” Samuel asked. “Saul will hear of it and kill me!”
units.rightText: And Samuel said, How can I go? if Saul hear it, he will kill me. And Jehovah said, Take a heifer with thee, and say, I am come to sacrifice to Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will show you what you are to do. You are to anoint for Me the one I indicate.”
units.rightText: And call Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will show thee what thou shalt do: and thou shalt anoint unto me him whom I name unto thee.

units.leftText: So Samuel did what the LORD had said and went to Bethlehem. When the elders of the town met him, they trembled and asked, “Do you come in peace?”
units.rightText: And Samuel did that which Jehovah spake, and came to Beth-lehem. And the elders of the city came to meet him trembling, and said, Comest thou peaceably?

units.leftText: “In peace,” he replied. “I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Consecrate yourselves and come with me to the sacrifice.”
units.rightText: And he said, Peaceably; I am come to sacrifice unto Jehovah: sanctify yourselves, and come with me to the sacrifice. And he sanctified Jesse and his sons, and called them to the sacrifice.

units.leftText: When they arrived, Samuel saw Eliab and said, “Surely here before the LORD is His anointed.”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when they were come, that he looked on Eliab, and said, Surely Jehovah’s anointed is before him.

units.leftText: But the LORD said to Samuel, “Do not consider his appearance or height, for I have rejected him; the LORD does not see as man does. For man sees the outward appearance, but the LORD sees the heart.”
units.rightText: But Jehovah said unto Samuel, Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have rejected him: for Jehovah seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but Jehovah looketh on the heart.

units.leftText: Then Jesse called Abinadab and presented him to Samuel, who said, “The LORD has not chosen this one either.”
units.rightText: Then Jesse called Abinadab, and made him pass before Samuel. And he said, Neither hath Jehovah chosen this.

units.leftText: Next Jesse presented Shammah, but Samuel said, “The LORD has not chosen this one either.”
units.rightText: Then Jesse made Shammah to pass by. And he said, Neither hath Jehovah chosen this.
leftNotes: 16:9 Shammah is a variant of Shimeah, Shimea, and Shimei; see 2 Samuel 13:3|2SA 13:3*, 2 Samuel 21:21, and 1 Chronicles 2:13.

units.leftText: Thus Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel, but Samuel told him, “The LORD has not chosen any of these.”
units.rightText: And Jesse made seven of his sons to pass before Samuel. And Samuel said unto Jesse, Jehovah hath not chosen these.

units.leftText: And Samuel asked him, “Are these all the sons you have?” “There is still the youngest,” Jesse replied, “but he is tending the sheep.” “Send for him,” Samuel replied. “For we will not sit down to eat until he arrives.”
units.rightText: And Samuel said unto Jesse, Are here all thy children? And he said, There remaineth yet the youngest, and, behold, he is keeping the sheep. And Samuel said unto Jesse, Send and fetch him; for we will not sit down till he come hither.

units.leftText: So Jesse sent for his youngest son and brought him in. He was ruddy, with beautiful eyes and a handsome appearance. And the LORD said, “Rise and anoint him, for he is the one.”
units.rightText: And he sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, and withal of a beautiful countenance, and goodly to look upon. And Jehovah said, Arise, anoint him; for this is he.

units.leftText: So Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the presence of his brothers, and the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon David from that day forward. Then Samuel set out and went to Ramah. David Serves Saul
units.rightText: Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brethren: and the Spirit of Jehovah came mightily upon David from that day forward. So Samuel rose up, and went to Ramah.

units.leftText: Now the Spirit of the LORD departed from Saul, and a spirit of distress from the LORD began to torment him.
units.rightText: Now the Spirit of Jehovah departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from Jehovah troubled him.
leftNotes: 16:14 Or a harmful spirit; similarly in verses 15, 16, and 23

units.leftText: Saul’s servants said to him, “Surely a spirit of distress from God is tormenting you.
units.rightText: And Saul’s servants said unto him, Behold now, an evil spirit from God troubleth thee.

units.leftText: Let our lord command your servants here to seek out someone who can skillfully play the harp. Whenever the spirit of distress from God is upon you, he is to play it, and you will be well.”
units.rightText: Let our lord now command thy servants, that are before thee, to seek out a man who is a skilful player on the harp: and it shall come to pass, when the evil spirit from God is upon thee, that he shall play with his hand, and thou shalt be well.

units.leftText: And Saul commanded his servants, “Find me someone who plays well, and bring him to me.”
units.rightText: And Saul said unto his servants, Provide me now a man that can play well, and bring him to me.

units.leftText: One of the servants answered, “I have seen a son of Jesse of Bethlehem who knows how to play the harp. He is a mighty man of valor, a warrior, eloquent and handsome, and the LORD is with him.”
units.rightText: Then answered one of the young men, and said, Behold, I have seen a son of Jesse the Beth-lehemite, that is skilful in playing, and a mighty man of valor, and a man of war, and prudent in speech, and a comely person; and Jehovah is with him.

units.leftText: So Saul sent messengers to Jesse and said, “Send me your son David, who is with the sheep.”
units.rightText: Wherefore Saul sent messengers unto Jesse, and said, Send me David thy son, who is with the sheep.

units.leftText: And Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread, a skin of wine, and one young goat and sent them to Saul with his son David.
units.rightText: And Jesse took an ass laden with bread, and a bottle of wine, and a kid, and sent them by David his son unto Saul.

units.leftText: When David came to Saul and entered his service, Saul loved him very much, and David became his armor-bearer.
units.rightText: And David came to Saul, and stood before him: and he loved him greatly; and he became his armorbearer.

units.leftText: Then Saul sent word to Jesse, saying, “Let David remain in my service, for I am pleased with him.”
units.rightText: And Saul sent to Jesse, saying, Let David, I pray thee, stand before me; for he hath found favor in my sight.

units.leftText: And whenever the spirit from God came upon Saul, David would pick up his harp and play. Then Saul would find relief and feel better, and the spirit of distress would depart from him.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when the evil spirit from God was upon Saul, that David took the harp, and played with his hand: so Saul was refreshed, and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him.

units.leftText: Now the Philistines gathered their forces for war at Socoh in Judah, and they camped between Socoh and Azekah in Ephes-dammim.
units.rightText: Now the Philistines gathered together their armies to battle; and they were gathered together at Socoh, which belongeth to Judah, and encamped between Socoh and Azekah, in Ephes-dammim.

units.leftText: Saul and the men of Israel assembled and camped in the Valley of Elah, arraying themselves for battle against the Philistines.
units.rightText: And Saul and the men of Israel were gathered together, and encamped in the vale of Elah, and set the battle in array against the Philistines.

units.leftText: The Philistines stood on one hill and the Israelites stood on another, with the valley between them.
units.rightText: And the Philistines stood on the mountain on the one side, and Israel stood on the mountain on the other side: and there was a valley between them.

units.leftText: Then a champion named Goliath, who was from Gath, came out from the Philistine camp. He was six cubits and a span in height,
units.rightText: And there went out a champion out of the camp of the Philistines, named Goliath, of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span.
leftNotes: 17:4 Goliath was approximately 9 feet 9 inches or 297 centimeters tall; LXX, DSS, and Josephus four cubits and a span in height (approximately 6 feet 9 inches or 206 centimeters tall).

units.leftText: and he had a bronze helmet on his head. He wore a bronze coat of mail weighing five thousand shekels,
units.rightText: And he had a helmet of brass upon his head, and he was clad with a coat of mail; and the weight of the coat was five thousand shekels of brass.
leftNotes: 17:5 5,000 shekels is approximately 125.6 pounds or 57 kilograms.

units.leftText: and he had armor of bronze on his legs and a javelin of bronze slung between his shoulders.
units.rightText: And he had greaves of brass upon his legs, and a javelin of brass between his shoulders.

units.leftText: The shaft of his spear was like a weaver’s beam, and its iron point weighed six hundred shekels. In addition, his shield bearer went before him.
units.rightText: And the staff of his spear was like a weaver’s beam; and his spear’s head weighed six hundred shekels of iron: and his shield-bearer went before him.
leftNotes: 17:7 600 shekels is approximately 15.1 pounds or 6.8 kilograms.

units.leftText: And Goliath stood and shouted to the ranks of Israel, “Why do you come out and array yourselves for battle? Am I not a Philistine, and are you not servants of Saul? Choose one of your men and have him come down against me.
units.rightText: And he stood and cried unto the armies of Israel, and said unto them, Why are ye come out to set your battle in array? am not I a Philistine, and ye servants to Saul? choose you a man for you, and let him come down to me.

units.leftText: If he is able to fight me and kill me, then we will be your servants. But if I prevail against him and kill him, then you shall be our servants and work for us.”
units.rightText: If he be able to fight with me, and kill me, then will we be your servants; but if I prevail against him, and kill him, then shall ye be our servants, and serve us.

units.leftText: Then the Philistine said, “I defy the ranks of Israel this day! Give me a man to fight!”
units.rightText: And the Philistine said, I defy the armies of Israel this day; give me a man, that we may fight together.

units.leftText: On hearing the words of the Philistine, Saul and all the Israelites were dismayed and greatly afraid. David Accepts the Challenge
units.rightText: And when Saul and all Israel heard those words of the Philistine, they were dismayed, and greatly afraid.

units.leftText: Now David was the son of a man named Jesse, an Ephrathite from Bethlehem of Judah who had eight sons. And in the days of Saul, Jesse was old and well along in years.
units.rightText: Now David was the son of that Ephrathite of Beth-lehem-judah, whose name was Jesse; and he had eight sons: and the man was an old man in the days of Saul, stricken in years among men.
leftNotes: 17:12 LXX and Syriac; Hebrew he had become advanced among men

units.leftText: The three older sons of Jesse had followed Saul into battle: The firstborn was Eliab, the second was Abinadab, and the third was Shammah.
units.rightText: And the three eldest sons of Jesse had gone after Saul to the battle: and the names of his three sons that went to the battle were Eliab the first-born, and next unto him Abinadab, and the third Shammah.

units.leftText: And David was the youngest.
units.rightText: And David was the youngest; and the three eldest followed Saul.

units.leftText: but David went back and forth from Saul to tend his father’s sheep in Bethlehem.
units.rightText: Now David went to and fro from Saul to feed his father’s sheep at Beth-lehem.

units.leftText: For forty days the Philistine came forward every morning and evening to take his stand.
units.rightText: And the Philistine drew near morning and evening, and presented himself forty days.

units.leftText: One day Jesse said to his son David, “Take this ephah of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread for your brothers and hurry to their camp.
units.rightText: And Jesse said unto David his son, Take now for thy brethren an ephah of this parched grain, and these ten loaves, and carry them quickly to the camp to thy brethren;
leftNotes: 17:17 An ephah is approximately 20 dry quarts or 22 liters of roasted grain.

units.leftText: Take also these ten portions of cheese to the commander of their unit. Check on the welfare of your brothers and bring back an assurance from them.
units.rightText: and bring these ten cheeses unto the captain of their thousand, and look how thy brethren fare, and take their pledge.
leftNotes: 17:18 Or some token from them or some pledge from them

units.leftText: They are with Saul and all the men of Israel in the Valley of Elah, fighting against the Philistines.”
units.rightText: Now Saul, and they, and all the men of Israel, were in the vale of Elah, fighting with the Philistines.

units.leftText: So David got up early in the morning, left the flock with a keeper, loaded up, and set out as Jesse had instructed him. He reached the camp as the army was marching out to its position and shouting the battle cry.
units.rightText: And David rose up early in the morning, and left the sheep with a keeper, and took, and went, as Jesse had commanded him; and he came to the place of the wagons, as the host which was going forth to the fight shouted for the battle.

units.leftText: And Israel and the Philistines arrayed in formation against each other.
units.rightText: And Israel and the Philistines put the battle in array, army against army.

units.leftText: Then David left his supplies in the care of the quartermaster and ran to the battle line. When he arrived, he asked his brothers how they were doing.
units.rightText: And David left his baggage in the hand of the keeper of the baggage, and ran to the army, and came and saluted his brethren.

units.leftText: And as he was speaking with them, suddenly the champion named Goliath, the Philistine from Gath, came forward from the ranks of the Philistines and shouted his usual words, which David also heard.
units.rightText: And as he talked with them, behold, there came up the champion, the Philistine of Gath, Goliath by name, out of the ranks of the Philistines, and spake according to the same words: and David heard them.

units.leftText: When all the men of Israel saw Goliath, they fled from him in great fear.
units.rightText: And all the men of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from him, and were sore afraid.

units.leftText: Now the men of Israel had been saying, “Do you see how this man keeps coming out to defy Israel? To the man who kills him the king will give great riches. And he will give him his daughter in marriage and exempt his father’s house from taxation in Israel.”
units.rightText: And the men of Israel said, Have ye seen this man that is come up? surely to defy Israel is he come up: and it shall be, that the man who killeth him, the king will enrich him with great riches, and will give him his daughter, and make his father’s house free in Israel.

units.leftText: David asked the men who were standing with him, “What will be done for the man who kills this Philistine and removes this disgrace from Israel? Just who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?”
units.rightText: And David spake to the men that stood by him, saying, What shall be done to the man that killeth this Philistine, and taketh away the reproach from Israel? for who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?

units.leftText: The people told him about the offer, saying, “That is what will be done for the man who kills him.”
units.rightText: And the people answered him after this manner, saying, So shall it be done to the man that killeth him.

units.leftText: Now when David’s oldest brother Eliab heard him speaking to the men, his anger burned against David. “Why have you come down here?” he asked. “And with whom did you leave those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your pride and wickedness of heart — you have come down to see the battle!”
units.rightText: And Eliab his eldest brother heard when he spake unto the men; and Eliab’s anger was kindled against David, and he said, Why art thou come down? and with whom hast thou left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know thy pride, and the naughtiness of thy heart; for thou art come down that thou mightest see the battle.

units.leftText: “What have I done now?” said David. “Was it not just a question?”
units.rightText: And David said, What have I now done? Is there not a cause?

units.leftText: Then he turned from him toward another and asked about the offer, and those people answered him just as the first ones had answered.
units.rightText: And he turned away from him toward another, and spake after the same manner: and the people answered him again after the former manner.

units.leftText: Now David’s words were overheard and reported to Saul, who sent for him.
units.rightText: And when the words were heard which David spake, they rehearsed them before Saul; and he sent for him.

units.leftText: And David said to Saul, “Let no man’s heart fail on account of this Philistine. Your servant will go and fight him!”
units.rightText: And David said to Saul, Let no man’s heart fail because of him; thy servant will go and fight with this Philistine.

units.leftText: But Saul replied, “You cannot go out against this Philistine to fight him. You are just a boy, and he has been a warrior from his youth.”
units.rightText: And Saul said to David, Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him; for thou art but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth.

units.leftText: David replied, “Your servant has been tending his father’s sheep, and whenever a lion or a bear came and carried off a lamb from the flock,
units.rightText: And David said unto Saul, Thy servant was keeping his father’s sheep; and when there came a lion, or a bear, and took a lamb out of the flock,

units.leftText: I went after it, struck it down, and delivered the lamb from its mouth. If it reared up against me, I would grab it by its fur, strike it down, and kill it.
units.rightText: I went out after him, and smote him, and delivered it out of his mouth; and when he arose against me, I caught him by his beard, and smote him, and slew him.

units.leftText: Your servant has killed lions and bears; this uncircumcised Philistine will be like one of them, for he has defied the armies of the living God.”
units.rightText: Thy servant smote both the lion and the bear: and this uncircumcised Philistine shall be as one of them, seeing he hath defied the armies of the living God.

units.leftText: David added, “The LORD, who delivered me from the claws of the lion and the bear, will deliver me from the hand of this Philistine.” “Go,” said Saul, “and may the LORD be with you.” David Slays Goliath
units.rightText: And David said, Jehovah that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine. And Saul said unto David, Go, and Jehovah shall be with thee.

units.leftText: Then Saul clothed David in his own tunic, put a bronze helmet on his head, and dressed him in armor.
units.rightText: And Saul clad David with his apparel, and he put a helmet of brass upon his head, and he clad him with a coat of mail.

units.leftText: David strapped his sword over the tunic and tried to walk, but he was not accustomed to them.
units.rightText: And David girded his sword upon his apparel, and he assayed to go; for he had not proved it. And David said unto Saul, I cannot go with these; for I have not proved them. And David put them off him.

units.leftText: And David took his staff in his hand, selected five smooth stones from the brook, and put them in the pouch of his shepherd’s bag. And with his sling in hand, he approached the Philistine.
units.rightText: And he took his staff in his hand, and chose him five smooth stones out of the brook, and put them in the shepherd’s bag which he had, even in his wallet; and his sling was in his hand: and he drew near to the Philistine.

units.leftText: Now the Philistine came closer and closer to David, with his shield-bearer before him.
units.rightText: And the Philistine came on and drew near unto David; and the man that bare the shield went before him.

units.leftText: When the Philistine looked and saw David, he despised him because he was just a boy, ruddy and handsome.
units.rightText: And when the Philistine looked about, and saw David, he disdained him; for he was but a youth, and ruddy, and withal of a fair countenance.

units.leftText: “Am I a dog,” he said to David, “that you come at me with sticks?” And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.
units.rightText: And the Philistine said unto David, Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves? And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.

units.leftText: “Come here,” he called to David, “and I will give your flesh to the birds of the air and the beasts of the field!”
units.rightText: And the Philistine said to David, Come to me, and I will give thy flesh unto the birds of the heavens, and to the beasts of the field.

units.leftText: But David said to the Philistine, “You come against me with sword and spear and javelin, but I come against you in the name of the LORD of Hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied.
units.rightText: Then said David to the Philistine, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a javelin: but I come to thee in the name of Jehovah of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.

units.leftText: This day the LORD will deliver you into my hand. This day I will strike you down, cut off your head, and give the carcasses of the Philistine army to the birds of the air and the creatures of the earth. Then the whole world will know that there is a God in Israel.
units.rightText: This day will Jehovah deliver thee into my hand; and I will smite thee, and take thy head from off thee; and I will give the dead bodies of the host of the Philistines this day unto the birds of the heavens, and to the wild beasts of the earth; that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel,

units.leftText: And all those assembled here will know that it is not by sword or spear that the LORD saves; for the battle is the LORD’s, and He will give all of you into our hands.”
units.rightText: and that all this assembly may know that Jehovah saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is Jehovah’s, and he will give you into our hand.

units.leftText: As the Philistine started forward to attack him, David ran quickly toward the battle line to meet him.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when the Philistine arose, and came and drew nigh to meet David, that David hastened, and ran toward the army to meet the Philistine.
