units.leftText: Then David reached into his bag, took out a stone, and slung it, striking the Philistine on the forehead. The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell facedown on the ground.
units.rightText: And David put his hand in his bag, and took thence a stone, and slang it, and smote the Philistine in his forehead; and the stone sank into his forehead, and he fell upon his face to the earth.

units.leftText: Thus David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and a stone; without a sword in his hand he struck down the Philistine and killed him.
units.rightText: So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone, and smote the Philistine, and slew him; but there was no sword in the hand of David.

units.leftText: David ran and stood over him. He grabbed the Philistine’s sword and pulled it from its sheath and killed him, and he cut off his head with the sword.
units.rightText: Then David ran, and stood over the Philistine, and took his sword, and drew it out of the sheath thereof, and slew him, and cut off his head therewith. And when the Philistines saw that their champion was dead, they fled.

units.leftText: Then the men of Israel and Judah charged forward with a shout and pursued the Philistines to the entrance of Gath and to the gates of Ekron. And the bodies of the Philistines were strewn along the Shaaraim road to Gath and Ekron.
units.rightText: And the men of Israel and of Judah arose, and shouted, and pursued the Philistines, until thou comest to Gai, and to the gates of Ekron. And the wounded of the Philistines fell down by the way to Shaaraim, even unto Gath, and unto Ekron.
leftNotes: 17:52 LXX; Hebrew of Gai; that is, of the valley

units.leftText: When the Israelites returned from their pursuit of the Philistines, they plundered their camps.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel returned from chasing after the Philistines, and they plundered their camp.

units.leftText: David took the head of the Philistine and brought it to Jerusalem, and he put Goliath’s weapons in his own tent.
units.rightText: And David took the head of the Philistine, and brought it to Jerusalem; but he put his armor in his tent.

units.leftText: As Saul had watched David going out to confront the Philistine, he said to Abner the commander of the army, “Abner, whose son is this young man?” “As surely as you live, O king,” Abner replied, “I do not know.”
units.rightText: And when Saul saw David go forth against the Philistine, he said unto Abner, the captain of the host, Abner, whose son is this youth? And Abner said, As thy soul liveth, O king, I cannot tell.

units.leftText: “Find out whose son this young man is!” said the king.
units.rightText: And the king said, Inquire thou whose son the stripling is.

units.leftText: So when David returned from killing the Philistine, still holding his head in his hand, Abner took him and brought him before Saul.
units.rightText: And as David returned from the slaughter of the Philistine, Abner took him, and brought him before Saul with the head of the Philistine in his hand.

units.leftText: “Whose son are you, young man?” asked Saul. “I am the son of your servant Jesse of Bethlehem,” David replied.
units.rightText: And Saul said to him, Whose son art thou, thou young man? And David answered, I am the son of thy servant Jesse the Beth-lehemite.

units.leftText: After David had finished speaking with Saul, the souls of Jonathan and David were knit together, and Jonathan loved him as himself.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking unto Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.

units.leftText: And from that day Saul kept David with him and did not let him return to his father’s house.
units.rightText: And Saul took him that day, and would let him go no more home to his father’s house.

units.leftText: Then Jonathan made a covenant with David because he loved him as himself.
units.rightText: Then Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul.

units.leftText: And Jonathan removed the robe he was wearing and gave it to David, along with his tunic, his sword, his bow, and his belt. Saul Envies David
units.rightText: And Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that was upon him, and gave it to David, and his apparel, even to his sword, and to his bow, and to his girdle.

units.leftText: So David marched out and prospered in everything Saul sent him to do, and Saul set him over the men of war. And this was pleasing in the sight of all the people, and of Saul’s officers as well.
units.rightText: And David went out whithersoever Saul sent him, and behaved himself wisely: and Saul set him over the men of war, and it was good in the sight of all the people, and also in the sight of Saul’s servants.

units.leftText: As the troops were returning home after David had killed the Philistine, the women came out of all the cities of Israel to meet King Saul with singing and dancing, with joyful songs, and with tambourines and other instruments.
units.rightText: And it came to pass as they came, when David returned from the slaughter of the Philistine, that the women came out of all the cities of Israel, singing and dancing, to meet king Saul, with timbrels, with joy, and with instruments of music.
leftNotes: 18:6 Possibly three-stringed instruments or cymbals or lutes or lyres

units.leftText: And as the women danced, they sang out: “Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands.”
units.rightText: And the women sang one to another as they played, and said, Saul hath slain his thousands, And David his ten thousands.

units.leftText: And Saul was furious and resented this song. “They have ascribed tens of thousands to David,” he said, “but only thousands to me. What more can he have but the kingdom?”
units.rightText: And Saul was very wroth, and this saying displeased him; and he said, They have ascribed unto David ten thousands, and to me they have ascribed but thousands: and what can he have more but the kingdom?

units.leftText: And from that day forward Saul kept a jealous eye on David.
units.rightText: And Saul eyed David from that day and forward.

units.leftText: The next day a spirit of distress sent from God came upon Saul, and he prophesied inside the house while David played the harp as usual. Now Saul was holding a spear,
units.rightText: And it came to pass on the morrow, that an evil spirit from God came mightily upon Saul, and he prophesied in the midst of the house: and David played with his hand, as he did day by day. And Saul had his spear in his hand;
leftNotes: 18:10 Or a harmful spirit

units.leftText: and he hurled it, thinking, “I will pin David to the wall.” But David eluded him twice.
units.rightText: and Saul cast the spear; for he said, I will smite David even to the wall. And David avoided out of his presence twice.

units.leftText: So Saul was afraid of David, because the LORD was with David but had departed from Saul.
units.rightText: And Saul was afraid of David, because Jehovah was with him, and was departed from Saul.

units.leftText: Therefore Saul sent David away and gave him command of a thousand men. David led the troops out to battle and back,
units.rightText: Therefore Saul removed him from him, and made him his captain over a thousand; and he went out and came in before the people.

units.leftText: and he continued to prosper in all his ways, because the LORD was with him.
units.rightText: And David behaved himself wisely in all his ways; and Jehovah was with him.

units.leftText: When Saul saw that David was very successful, he was afraid of him.
units.rightText: And when Saul saw that he behaved himself very wisely, he stood in awe of him.

units.leftText: But all Israel and Judah loved David, because he was leading them out to battle and back. David Marries Michal
units.rightText: But all Israel and Judah loved David; for he went out and came in before them.

units.leftText: Then Saul said to David, “Here is my older daughter Merab. I will give her to you in marriage. Only be valiant for me and fight the LORD’s battles.” But Saul was thinking, “I need not raise my hand against him; let the hand of the Philistines be against him.”
units.rightText: And Saul said to David, Behold, my elder daughter Merab, her will I give thee to wife: only be thou valiant for me, and fight Jehovah’s battles. For Saul said, Let not my hand be upon him, but let the hand of the Philistines be upon him.

units.leftText: And David said to Saul, “Who am I, and what is my family or my father’s clan in Israel, that I should become the son-in-law of the king?”
units.rightText: And David said unto Saul, Who am I, and what is my life, or my father’s family in Israel, that I should be son-in-law to the king?

units.leftText: So when it was time to give Saul’s daughter Merab to David, she was given in marriage to Adriel of Meholah.
units.rightText: But it came to pass at the time when Merab, Saul’s daughter, should have been given to David, that she was given unto Adriel the Meholathite to wife.
leftNotes: 18:19 Or But when it was time

units.leftText: Now Saul’s daughter Michal loved David, and when this was reported to Saul, it pleased him.
units.rightText: And Michal, Saul’s daughter, loved David: and they told Saul, and the thing pleased him.

units.leftText: “I will give her to David,” Saul thought, “so that she may be a snare to him, and the hand of the Philistines may be against him.” So Saul said to David, “For a second time now you can be my son-in-law.”
units.rightText: And Saul said, I will give him her, that she may be a snare to him, and that the hand of the Philistines may be against him. Wherefore Saul said to David, Thou shalt this day be my son-in-law a second time.

units.leftText: Then Saul ordered his servants, “Speak to David privately and tell him, ‘Behold, the king is pleased with you, and all his servants love you. Now therefore, become his son-in-law.’”
units.rightText: And Saul commanded his servants, saying, Commune with David secretly, and say, Behold, the king hath delight in thee, and all his servants love thee: now therefore be the king’s son-in-law.

units.leftText: But when Saul’s servants relayed these words to David, he replied, “Does it seem trivial in your sight to be the son-in-law of the king? I am a poor man and lightly esteemed.”
units.rightText: And Saul’s servants spake those words in the ears of David. And David said, Seemeth it to you a light thing to be the king’s son-in-law, seeing that I am a poor man, and lightly esteemed?

units.leftText: And the servants told Saul what David had said.
units.rightText: And the servants of Saul told him, saying, On this manner spake David.

units.leftText: Saul replied, “Say to David, ‘The king desires no other dowry but a hundred Philistine foreskins as revenge on his enemies.’” But Saul intended to cause David’s death at the hands of the Philistines.
units.rightText: And Saul said, Thus shall ye say to David, The king desireth not any dowry, but a hundred foreskins of the Philistines, to be avenged of the king’s enemies. Now Saul thought to make David fall by the hand of the Philistines.

units.leftText: When the servants reported these terms to David, he was pleased to become the king’s son-in-law. Before the wedding day arrived,
units.rightText: And when his servants told David these words, it pleased David well to be the king’s son-in-law. And the days were not expired;

units.leftText: David and his men went out and killed two hundred Philistines. He brought their foreskins and presented them as payment in full to become the king’s son-in-law. Then Saul gave his daughter Michal to David in marriage.
units.rightText: and David arose and went, he and his men, and slew of the Philistines two hundred men; and David brought their foreskins, and they gave them in full number to the king, that he might be the king’s son-in-law. And Saul gave him Michal his daughter to wife.

units.leftText: When Saul realized that the LORD was with David and that his daughter Michal loved David,
units.rightText: And Saul saw and knew that Jehovah was with David; and Michal, Saul’s daughter, loved him.

units.leftText: he grew even more afraid of David. So from then on Saul was David’s enemy.
units.rightText: And Saul was yet the more afraid of David; and Saul was David’s enemy continually.

units.leftText: Every time the Philistine commanders came out for battle, David was more successful than all of Saul’s officers, so that his name was highly esteemed.
units.rightText: Then the princes of the Philistines went forth: and it came to pass, as often as they went forth, that David behaved himself more wisely than all the servants of Saul; so that his name was much set by.

units.leftText: Then Saul ordered his son Jonathan and all his servants to kill David.
units.rightText: And Saul spake to Jonathan his son, and to all his servants, that they should slay David. But Jonathan, Saul’s son, delighted much in David.

units.leftText: so he warned David, saying, “My father Saul intends to kill you. Be on your guard in the morning; find a secret place and hide there.
units.rightText: And Jonathan told David, saying, Saul my father seeketh to slay thee: now therefore, I pray thee, take heed to thyself in the morning, and abide in a secret place, and hide thyself:

units.leftText: I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are, so I can ask about you. And if I find out anything, I will tell you.”
units.rightText: and I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where thou art, and I will commune with my father of thee; and if I see aught, I will tell thee.

units.leftText: Then Jonathan spoke well of David to his father Saul and said to him, “The king should not sin against his servant David; he has not sinned against you. In fact, his actions have been highly beneficial to you.
units.rightText: And Jonathan spake good of David unto Saul his father, and said unto him, Let not the king sin against his servant, against David; because he hath not sinned against thee, and because his works have been to thee-ward very good:

units.leftText: He took his life in his hands when he struck down the Philistine, and the LORD worked a great salvation for all Israel. You saw it and rejoiced, so why would you sin against innocent blood by killing David for no reason?”
units.rightText: for he put his life in his hand, and smote the Philistine, and Jehovah wrought a great victory for all Israel: thou sawest it, and didst rejoice; wherefore then wilt thou sin against innocent blood, to slay David without a cause?

units.leftText: Saul listened to the voice of Jonathan and swore an oath: “As surely as the LORD lives, David will not be put to death.”
units.rightText: And Saul hearkened unto the voice of Jonathan: and Saul sware, As Jehovah liveth, he shall not be put to death.

units.leftText: So Jonathan summoned David and told him all these things. Then Jonathan brought David to Saul, and David was with Saul as before.
units.rightText: And Jonathan called David, and Jonathan showed him all those things. And Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he was in his presence, as beforetime.

units.leftText: When war broke out again, David went out and fought the Philistines and struck them with such a mighty blow that they fled before him.
units.rightText: And there was war again: and David went out, and fought with the Philistines, and slew them with a great slaughter; and they fled before him.

units.leftText: But as Saul was sitting in his house with his spear in his hand, a spirit of distress from the LORD came upon him. While David was playing the harp,
units.rightText: And an evil spirit from Jehovah was upon Saul, as he sat in his house with his spear in his hand; and David was playing with his hand.
leftNotes: 19:9 Or a harmful spirit

units.leftText: Saul tried to pin him to the wall with his spear. But David eluded him and the spear struck the wall. And David fled and escaped that night.
units.rightText: And Saul sought to smite David even to the wall with the spear; but he slipped away out of Saul’s presence, and he smote the spear into the wall: and David fled, and escaped that night.

units.leftText: Then Saul sent messengers to David’s house to watch him and kill him in the morning. But David’s wife Michal warned him, “If you do not run for your life tonight, tomorrow you will be dead!”
units.rightText: And Saul sent messengers unto David’s house, to watch him, and to slay him in the morning: and Michal, David’s wife, told him, saying, If thou save not thy life to-night, to-morrow thou wilt be slain.

units.leftText: So Michal lowered David from the window, and he ran away and escaped.
units.rightText: So Michal let David down through the window: and he went, and fled, and escaped.

units.leftText: Then Michal took a household idol and laid it in the bed, placed some goat hair on its head, and covered it with a garment.
units.rightText: And Michal took the teraphim, and laid it in the bed, and put a pillow of goats’ hair at the head thereof, and covered it with the clothes.
leftNotes: 19:13 Or a household god; Hebrew teraphim; also in verse 16

units.leftText: When Saul sent the messengers to seize David, Michal said, “He is ill.”
units.rightText: And when Saul sent messengers to take David, she said, He is sick.

units.leftText: But Saul sent the messengers back to see David and told them, “Bring him up to me in his bed so I can kill him.”
units.rightText: And Saul sent the messengers to see David, saying, Bring him up to me in the bed, that I may slay him.

units.leftText: And when the messengers entered, there was the idol in the bed with the goat hair on its head.
units.rightText: And when the messengers came in, behold, the teraphim was in the bed, with the pillow of goats’ hair at the head thereof.

units.leftText: And Saul said to Michal, “Why did you deceive me like this? You sent my enemy away, and he has escaped!” Michal replied, “He said to me, ‘Help me get away, or I will kill you!’”
units.rightText: And Saul said unto Michal, Why hast thou deceived me thus, and let mine enemy go, so that he is escaped? And Michal answered Saul, He said unto me, Let me go; why should I kill thee?

units.leftText: So David ran away and escaped. And he went to Samuel at Ramah and told him all that Saul had done to him. Then he and Samuel went to Naioth and stayed there.
units.rightText: Now David fled, and escaped, and came to Samuel to Ramah, and told him all that Saul had done to him. And he and Samuel went and dwelt in Naioth.

units.leftText: When Saul was told that David was at Naioth in Ramah,
units.rightText: And it was told Saul, saying, Behold, David is at Naioth in Ramah.

units.leftText: he sent messengers to seize him. But when they saw the group of prophets prophesying, with Samuel leading them, the Spirit of God came upon them, and Saul’s messengers also began to prophesy.
units.rightText: And Saul sent messengers to take David: and when they saw the company of the prophets prophesying, and Samuel standing as head over them, the Spirit of God came upon the messengers of Saul, and they also prophesied.

units.leftText: When this was reported to Saul, he sent more messengers, but they began to prophesy as well. So Saul tried again and sent messengers a third time, and even they began to prophesy.
units.rightText: And when it was told Saul, he sent other messengers, and they also prophesied. And Saul sent messengers again the third time, and they also prophesied.

units.leftText: Finally, Saul himself left for Ramah and came to the large cistern at Secu, where he asked, “Where are Samuel and David?” “At Naioth in Ramah,” he was told.
units.rightText: Then went he also to Ramah, and came to the great well that is in Secu: and he asked and said, Where are Samuel and David? And one said, Behold, they are at Naioth in Ramah.

units.leftText: So Saul went to Naioth in Ramah. But the Spirit of God came upon even Saul, and he walked along prophesying until he came to Naioth in Ramah.
units.rightText: And he went thither to Naioth in Ramah: and the Spirit of God came upon him also, and he went on, and prophesied, until he came to Naioth in Ramah.

units.leftText: Then Saul stripped off his robes and also prophesied before Samuel. And he collapsed and lay naked all that day and night. That is why it is said, “Is Saul also among the prophets?”
units.rightText: And he also stripped off his clothes, and he also prophesied before Samuel, and lay down naked all that day and all that night. Wherefore they say, Is Saul also among the prophets?

units.leftText: Then David fled from Naioth in Ramah. He came to Jonathan and asked, “What have I done? What is my iniquity? How have I sinned against your father, that he wants to take my life?”
units.rightText: And David fled from Naioth in Ramah, and came and said before Jonathan, What have I done? what is mine iniquity? and what is my sin before thy father, that he seeketh my life?

units.leftText: “Far from it!” Jonathan replied. “You will not die. Indeed, my father does nothing, great or small, without telling me. So why would he hide this matter from me? This cannot be true!”
units.rightText: And he said unto him, Far from it; thou shalt not die: behold, my father doeth nothing either great or small, but that he discloseth it unto me; and why should my father hide this thing from me? it is not so.

units.leftText: But David again vowed, “Your father knows very well that I have found favor in your eyes, and he has said, ‘Jonathan must not know of this, or he will be grieved.’ As surely as the LORD lives and as you yourself live, there is but a step between me and death.”
units.rightText: And David sware moreover, and said, Thy father knoweth well that I have found favor in thine eyes; and he saith, Let not Jonathan know this, lest he be grieved: but truly as Jehovah liveth, and as thy soul liveth, there is but a step between me and death.

units.leftText: Then Jonathan said to David, “Whatever you desire, I will do for you.”
units.rightText: Then said Jonathan unto David, Whatsoever thy soul desireth, I will even do it for thee.

units.leftText: So David told him, “Look, tomorrow is the New Moon, and I am supposed to dine with the king. Instead, let me go and hide in the field until the third evening from now.
units.rightText: And David said unto Jonathan, Behold, to-morrow is the new moon, and I should not fail to sit with the king at meat: but let me go, that I may hide myself in the field unto the third day at even.
leftNotes: 20:5 That is, the New Moon feast; also in verses 18, 24, and 27

units.leftText: If your father misses me at all, tell him, ‘David urgently requested my permission to hurry to Bethlehem, his hometown, because there is an annual sacrifice for his whole clan.’
units.rightText: If thy father miss me at all, then say, David earnestly asked leave of me that he might run to Beth-lehem his city; for it is the yearly sacrifice there for all the family.

units.leftText: If he says, ‘Good,’ then your servant is safe, but if he is enraged, you will know he has evil intentions.
units.rightText: If he say thus, It is well; thy servant shall have peace: but if he be wroth, then know that evil is determined by him.

units.leftText: Therefore show kindness to your servant, for you have brought me into a covenant with you before the LORD. If there is iniquity in me, then kill me yourself; why should you bring me to your father?”
units.rightText: Therefore deal kindly with thy servant; for thou hast brought thy servant into a covenant of Jehovah with thee: but if there be in me iniquity, slay me thyself; for why shouldest thou bring me to thy father?

units.leftText: “Never!” Jonathan replied. “If I ever found out that my father had evil intentions against you, would I not tell you?” Jonathan and David Renew Their Covenant
units.rightText: And Jonathan said, Far be it from thee; for if I should at all know that evil were determined by my father to come upon thee, then would not I tell it thee?

units.leftText: Then David asked Jonathan, “Who will tell me if your father answers you harshly?”
units.rightText: Then said David to Jonathan, Who shall tell me if perchance thy father answer thee roughly?

units.leftText: “Come,” he replied, “let us go out to the field.”
units.rightText: And Jonathan said unto David, Come, and let us go out into the field. And they went out both of them into the field.

units.leftText: and Jonathan said, “By the LORD, the God of Israel, I will sound out my father by this time tomorrow or the next day. If he is favorable toward you, will I not send for you and tell you?
units.rightText: And Jonathan said unto David, Jehovah, the God of Israel, be witness: when I have sounded my father about this time to-morrow, or the third day, behold, if there be good toward David, shall I not then send unto thee, and disclose it unto thee?

units.leftText: But if my father intends to bring evil on you, then may the LORD punish me, and ever so severely, if I do not tell you and send you on your way in safety. May the LORD be with you, just as He has been with my father.
units.rightText: Jehovah do so to Jonathan, and more also, should it please my father to do thee evil, if I disclose it not unto thee, and send thee away, that thou mayest go in peace: and Jehovah be with thee, as he hath been with my father.

units.leftText: And as long as I live, treat me with the LORD’s loving devotion, that I may not die,
units.rightText: And thou shalt not only while yet I live show me the lovingkindness of Jehovah, that I die not;
leftNotes: 20:14 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: and do not ever cut off your loving devotion from my household— not even when the LORD cuts off every one of David’s enemies from the face of the earth.”
units.rightText: but also thou shalt not cut off thy kindness from my house for ever; no, not when Jehovah hath cut off the enemies of David every one from the face of the earth.

units.leftText: So Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David, saying, “May the LORD hold David’s enemies accountable.”
units.rightText: So Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David, saying, And Jehovah will require it at the hand of David’s enemies.

units.leftText: And Jonathan had David reaffirm his vow out of love for him, for Jonathan loved David as he loved himself.
units.rightText: And Jonathan caused David to swear again, for the love that he had to him; for he loved him as he loved his own soul.

units.leftText: Then Jonathan said to David, “Tomorrow is the New Moon, and you will be missed, because your seat will be empty.
units.rightText: Then Jonathan said unto him, To-morrow is the new moon: and thou wilt be missed, because thy seat will be empty.

units.leftText: When you have stayed three days, hurry down to the place you hid on the day this trouble began, and remain beside the stone Ezel.
units.rightText: And when thou hast stayed three days, thou shalt go down quickly, and come to the place where thou didst hide thyself when the business was in hand, and shalt remain by the stone Ezel.
leftNotes: 20:19 Ezel means departure.

units.leftText: I will shoot three arrows to the side of it, as if I were aiming at a target.
units.rightText: And I will shoot three arrows on the side thereof, as though I shot at a mark.

units.leftText: Then I will send a boy and say, ‘Go, find the arrows!’ Now, if I expressly say to him, ‘Look, the arrows are on this side of you; bring them,’ then come, because as surely as the LORD lives, it is safe for you, and there is no danger.
units.rightText: And, behold, I will send the lad, saying, Go, find the arrows. If I say unto the lad, Behold, the arrows are on this side of thee; take them, and come; for there is peace to thee and no hurt, as Jehovah liveth.

units.leftText: But if I say to the young man, ‘Look, the arrows are beyond you,’ then you must go, for the LORD has sent you away.
units.rightText: But if I say thus unto the boy, Behold, the arrows are beyond thee; go thy way; for Jehovah hath sent thee away.

units.leftText: And as for the matter you and I have discussed, the LORD is a witness between you and me forever.”
units.rightText: And as touching the matter which thou and I have spoken of, behold, Jehovah is between thee and me for ever.

units.leftText: So David hid in the field, and when the New Moon had come, the king sat down to eat.
units.rightText: So David hid himself in the field: and when the new moon was come, the king sat him down to eat food.

units.leftText: He sat in his usual place by the wall, opposite Jonathan and beside Abner, but David’s place was empty.
units.rightText: And the king sat upon his seat, as at other times, even upon the seat by the wall; and Jonathan stood up, and Abner sat by Saul’s side: but David’s place was empty.
leftNotes: 20:25 LXX; Hebrew by the wall. Jonathan arose and Abner sat down by Saul’s side,

units.leftText: Saul said nothing that day because he thought, “Something has happened to David to make him ceremonially unclean— surely he is unclean.”
units.rightText: Nevertheless Saul spake not anything that day: for he thought, Something hath befallen him, he is not clean; surely he is not clean.

units.leftText: But on the day after the New Moon, the second day, David’s place was still empty, and Saul asked his son Jonathan, “Why hasn’t the son of Jesse come to the meal either yesterday or today?”
units.rightText: And it came to pass on the morrow after the new moon, which was the second day, that David’s place was empty: and Saul said unto Jonathan his son, Wherefore cometh not the son of Jesse to meat, neither yesterday, nor to-day?

units.leftText: Jonathan answered, “David urgently requested my permission to go to Bethlehem,
units.rightText: And Jonathan answered Saul, David earnestly asked leave of me to go to Beth-lehem:

units.leftText: saying, ‘Please let me go, because our clan is holding a sacrifice in the city, and my brother has told me to be there. So now, if I have found favor in your eyes, please let me go and see my brothers.’ That is why he has not come to the king’s table.” Saul Seeks to Kill Jonathan
units.rightText: and he said, Let me go, I pray thee; for our family hath a sacrifice in the city; and my brother, he hath commanded me to be there: and now, if I have found favor in thine eyes, let me get away, I pray thee, and see my brethren. Therefore he is not come unto the king’s table.

units.leftText: Then Saul’s anger burned against Jonathan, and he said to him, “You son of a perverse and rebellious woman! Do I not know that you have chosen the son of Jesse to your own shame and to the shame of the mother who bore you?
units.rightText: Then Saul’s anger was kindled against Jonathan, and he said unto him, Thou son of a perverse rebellious woman, do not I know that thou hast chosen the son of Jesse to thine own shame, and unto the shame of thy mother’s nakedness?

units.leftText: For as long as the son of Jesse lives on this earth, neither you nor your kingdom shall be established. Now send for him and bring him to me, for he must surely die!”
units.rightText: For as long as the son of Jesse liveth upon the ground, thou shalt not be established, nor thy kingdom. Wherefore now send and fetch him unto me, for he shall surely die.

units.leftText: “Why must he be put to death?” Jonathan replied. “What has he done?”
units.rightText: And Jonathan answered Saul his father, and said unto him, Wherefore should he be put to death? what hath he done?

units.leftText: Then Saul hurled his spear at Jonathan to kill him. So Jonathan knew that his father was determined to kill David.
units.rightText: And Saul cast his spear at him to smite him; whereby Jonathan knew that it was determined of his father to put David to death.

units.leftText: Jonathan got up from the table in fierce anger and did not eat any food that second day of the month, for he was grieved by his father’s shameful treatment of David.
units.rightText: So Jonathan arose from the table in fierce anger, and did eat no food the second day of the month; for he was grieved for David, because his father had done him shame.

units.leftText: In the morning Jonathan went out to the field for the appointment with David, and a small boy was with him.
units.rightText: And it came to pass in the morning, that Jonathan went out into the field at the time appointed with David, and a little lad with him.

units.leftText: He said to the boy, “Run and find the arrows I shoot.” And as the boy ran, Jonathan shot an arrow beyond him.
units.rightText: And he said unto his lad, Run, find now the arrows which I shoot. And as the lad ran, he shot an arrow beyond him.

units.leftText: When the boy reached the place where Jonathan’s arrow had fallen, Jonathan called to him, “Isn’t the arrow beyond you?”
units.rightText: And when the lad was come to the place of the arrow which Jonathan had shot, Jonathan cried after the lad, and said, Is not the arrow beyond thee?

units.leftText: Then Jonathan cried out, “Hurry! Make haste! Do not delay!” So the boy picked up the arrow and returned to his master.
units.rightText: And Jonathan cried after the lad, Make speed, haste, stay not. And Jonathan’s lad gathered up the arrows, and came to his master.

units.leftText: But the boy did not know anything; only Jonathan and David knew the arrangement.
units.rightText: But the lad knew not anything: only Jonathan and David knew the matter.

units.leftText: Then Jonathan gave his equipment to the boy and said, “Go, take it back to the city.”
units.rightText: And Jonathan gave his weapons unto his lad, and said unto him, Go, carry them to the city.

units.leftText: When the young man had gone, David got up from the south side of the stone, fell facedown, and bowed three times. Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and wept together — though David wept more.
units.rightText: And as soon as the lad was gone, David arose out of a place toward the South, and fell on his face to the ground, and bowed himself three times: and they kissed one another, and wept one with another, until David exceeded.
leftNotes: 20:41 Hebrew from the south side; LXX from beside the stone

units.leftText: And Jonathan said to David, “Go in peace, for the two of us have sworn in the name of the LORD, saying, ‘May the LORD be a witness between you and me, and between your descendants and mine forever.’” Then David got up and departed, and Jonathan went back into the city.
units.rightText: And Jonathan said to David, Go in peace, forasmuch as we have sworn both of us in the name of Jehovah, saying, Jehovah shall be between me and thee, and between my seed and thy seed, for ever. And he arose and departed: and Jonathan went into the city.

units.leftText: Then David came to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest. And when Ahimelech met David, he trembled and asked him, “Why are you alone? Why is no one with you?”
units.rightText: Then came David to Nob to Ahimelech the priest: and Ahimelech came to meet David trembling, and said unto him, Why art thou alone, and no man with thee?

units.leftText: “The king has given me a mission,” David replied. “He told me no one is to know about the mission on which I am sending you. And I have directed my young men to meet me at a certain place.
units.rightText: And David said unto Ahimelech the priest, The king hath commanded me a business, and hath said unto me, Let no man know anything of the business whereabout I send thee, and what I have commanded thee: and I have appointed the young men to such and such a place.

units.leftText: Now then, what do you have on hand? Give me five loaves of bread, or whatever can be found.”
units.rightText: Now therefore what is under thy hand? give me five loaves of bread in my hand, or whatsoever there is present.

units.leftText: “There is no common bread on hand,” the priest replied, “but there is some consecrated bread — provided that the young men have kept themselves from women.”
units.rightText: And the priest answered David, and said, There is no common bread under my hand, but there is holy bread; if only the young men have kept themselves from women.

units.leftText: David answered, “Women have indeed been kept from us, as is usual when I set out. And the bodies of the young men are holy even on common missions. How much more so today!”
units.rightText: And David answered the priest, and said unto him, Of a truth women have been kept from us about these three days; when I came out, the vessels of the young men were holy, though it was but a common journey; how much more then to-day shall their vessels be holy?

units.leftText: So the priest gave him the consecrated bread, since there was no bread there but the Bread of the Presence, which had been removed from before the LORD and replaced with hot bread on the day it was taken away.
units.rightText: So the priest gave him holy bread; for there was no bread there but the showbread, that was taken from before Jehovah, to put hot bread in the day when it was taken away.

units.leftText: Now one of Saul’s servants was there that day, detained before the LORD. And his name was Doeg the Edomite, the chief shepherd for Saul. David Flees to Gath (Psalm 34:1–22|PSA 34:1-22*; Psalm 56:1–13|PSA 56:1-13*)
units.rightText: Now a certain man of the servants of Saul was there that day, detained before Jehovah; and his name was Doeg the Edomite, the chiefest of the herdsmen that belonged to Saul.

units.leftText: Then David asked Ahimelech, “Is there not a spear or sword on hand here? For I have brought neither my sword nor my weapons with me, because the king’s mission was urgent.”
units.rightText: And David said unto Ahimelech, And is there not here under thy hand spear or sword? for I have neither brought my sword nor my weapons with me, because the king’s business required haste.

units.leftText: The priest replied, “The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you killed in the Valley of Elah, is here; it is wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. If you want, you may take it. For there is no other but this one here.” And David said, “There is none like it; give it to me.”
units.rightText: And the priest said, The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom thou slewest in the vale of Elah, behold, it is here wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod: if thou wilt take that, take it; for there is no other save that here. And David said, There is none like that; give it me.

units.leftText: That day David fled from Saul and went to Achish king of Gath.
units.rightText: And David arose, and fled that day for fear of Saul, and went to Achish the king of Gath.

units.leftText: But the servants of Achish said to him, “Is this not David, the king of the land? Did they not sing about him in their dances, saying: ‘Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands’?”
units.rightText: And the servants of Achish said unto him, Is not this David the king of the land? did they not sing one to another of him in dances, saying, Saul hath slain his thousands, And David his ten thousands?

units.leftText: Now David took these words to heart and was very much afraid of Achish the king of Gath.
units.rightText: And David laid up these words in his heart, and was sore afraid of Achish the king of Gath.

units.leftText: So he changed his behavior before them and feigned madness in their hands; he scratched on the doors of the gate and let his saliva run down his beard.
units.rightText: And he changed his behavior before them, and feigned himself mad in their hands, and scrabbled on the doors of the gate, and let his spittle fall down upon his beard.

units.leftText: Then Achish said to his servants, “Look, you can see that the man is insane! Why have you brought him to me?
units.rightText: Then said Achish unto his servants, Lo, ye see the man is mad; wherefore then have ye brought him to me?

units.leftText: Am I in need of madmen, that you have brought this man to rave in my presence? Must this man come into my house?”
units.rightText: Do I lack madmen, that ye have brought this fellow to play the madman in my presence? shall this fellow come into my house?

units.leftText: So David left Gath and took refuge in the cave of Adullam. When his brothers and the rest of his father’s household heard about it, they went down to him there.
units.rightText: David therefore departed thence, and escaped to the cave of Adullam: and when his brethren and all his father’s house heard it, they went down thither to him.

units.leftText: And all who were distressed or indebted or discontented rallied around him, and he became their leader. About four hundred men were with him.
units.rightText: And every one that was in distress, and every one that was in debt, and every one that was discontented, gathered themselves unto him; and he became captain over them: and there were with him about four hundred men.

units.leftText: From there David went to Mizpeh of Moab, where he said to the king of Moab, “Please let my father and mother stay with you until I learn what God will do for me.”
units.rightText: And David went thence to Mizpeh of Moab: and he said unto the king of Moab, Let my father and my mother, I pray thee, come forth, and be with you, till I know what God will do for me.
leftNotes: 22:3 Syriac and Vulgate; Hebrew go forth

units.leftText: So he left them in the care of the king of Moab, and they stayed with him the whole time David was in the stronghold.
units.rightText: And he brought them before the king of Moab: and they dwelt with him all the while that David was in the stronghold.

units.leftText: Then the prophet Gad said to David, “Do not stay in the stronghold. Depart and go into the land of Judah.” So David left and went to the forest of Hereth. Saul Slays the Priests of Nob (Psalm 52:1–9|PSA 52:1-9*)
units.rightText: And the prophet Gad said unto David, Abide not in the stronghold; depart, and get thee into the land of Judah. Then David departed, and came into the forest of Hereth.

units.leftText: Soon Saul learned that David and his men had been discovered. At that time Saul was sitting under the tamarisk tree on the hill at Gibeah, with his spear in hand and all his servants standing around him.
units.rightText: And Saul heard that David was discovered, and the men that were with him: now Saul was sitting in Gibeah, under the tamarisk-tree in Ramah, with his spear in his hand, and all his servants were standing about him.

units.leftText: Then Saul said to his servants, “Listen, men of Benjamin! Is the son of Jesse giving all of you fields and vineyards and making you commanders of thousands or hundreds?
units.rightText: And Saul said unto his servants that stood about him, Hear now, ye Benjamites; will the son of Jesse give every one of you fields and vineyards, will he make you all captains of thousands and captains of hundreds,

units.leftText: Is that why all of you have conspired against me? Not one of you told me that my own son had made a covenant with the son of Jesse. Not one of you has shown concern for me or revealed to me that my son has stirred up my own servant to lie in wait against me, as is the case today.”
units.rightText: that all of you have conspired against me, and there is none that discloseth to me when my son maketh a league with the son of Jesse, and there is none of you that is sorry for me, or discloseth unto me that my son hath stirred up my servant against me, to lie in wait, as at this day?

units.leftText: But Doeg the Edomite, who had stationed himself with Saul’s servants, answered: “I saw the son of Jesse come to Ahimelech son of Ahitub at Nob.
units.rightText: Then answered Doeg the Edomite, who stood by the servants of Saul, and said, I saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.

units.leftText: Ahimelech inquired of the LORD for him and gave him provisions. He also gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.”
units.rightText: And he inquired of Jehovah for him, and gave him victuals, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.

units.leftText: Then the king sent messengers to summon Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and his father’s whole family, who were priests at Nob. And all of them came to the king.
units.rightText: Then the king sent to call Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and all his father’s house, the priests that were in Nob: and they came all of them to the king.

units.leftText: “Listen now, son of Ahitub,” said Saul. “Here I am, my lord,” he replied.
units.rightText: And Saul said, Hear now, thou son of Ahitub. And he answered, Here I am, my lord.

units.leftText: And Saul asked him, “Why have you and the son of Jesse conspired against me? You gave him bread and a sword and inquired of God for him so that he could rise up against me to lie in wait, as he is doing today.”
units.rightText: And Saul said unto him, Why have ye conspired against me, thou and the son of Jesse, in that thou hast given him bread, and a sword, and hast inquired of God for him, that he should rise against me, to lie in wait, as at this day?

units.leftText: Ahimelech answered the king, “Who among all your servants is as faithful as David, the king’s son-in-law, the captain of your bodyguard and honored in your house?
units.rightText: Then Ahimelech answered the king, and said, And who among all thy servants is so faithful as David, who is the king’s son-in-law, and is taken into thy council, and is honorable in thy house?

units.leftText: Was that day the first time I inquired of God for him? Far be it from me! Let not the king accuse your servant or any of my father’s household, for your servant knew nothing of this whole affair — not in part or in whole.”
units.rightText: Have I to-day begun to inquire of God for him? be it far from me: let not the king impute anything unto his servant, nor to all the house of my father; for thy servant knoweth nothing of all this, less or more.

units.leftText: But the king replied, “You will surely die, Ahimelech, you and all your father’s house!”
units.rightText: And the king said, Thou shalt surely die, Ahimelech, thou, and all thy father’s house.

units.leftText: Then the king ordered the guards at his side, “Turn and kill the priests of the LORD, because they too sided with David. For they knew he was fleeing, but they did not tell me.” But the king’s servants would not lift a hand to strike the priests of the LORD.
units.rightText: And the king said unto the guard that stood about him, Turn, and slay the priests of Jehovah; because their hand also is with David, and because they knew that he fled, and did not disclose it to me. But the servants of the king would not put forth their hand to fall upon the priests of Jehovah.

units.leftText: So the king ordered Doeg, “You turn and strike down the priests!”
units.rightText: And the king said to Doeg, Turn thou, and fall upon the priests. And Doeg the Edomite turned, and he fell upon the priests, and he slew on that day fourscore and five persons that did wear a linen ephod.

units.leftText: He also put to the sword Nob, the city of the priests, with its men and women, children and infants, oxen, donkeys, and sheep.
units.rightText: And Nob, the city of the priests, smote he with the edge of the sword, both men and women, children and sucklings, and oxen and asses and sheep, with the edge of the sword.

units.leftText: But one of the sons of Ahimelech son of Ahitub escaped. His name was Abiathar, and he fled to David.
units.rightText: And one of the sons of Ahimelech, the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped, and fled after David.

units.leftText: And Abiathar told David that Saul had killed the priests of the LORD.
units.rightText: And Abiathar told David that Saul had slain Jehovah’s priests.

units.leftText: Then David said to Abiathar, “I knew that Doeg the Edomite was there that day, and that he was sure to tell Saul. I myself am responsible for the lives of everyone in your father’s house.
units.rightText: And David said unto Abiathar, I knew on that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Saul: I have occasioned the death of all the persons of thy father’s house.

units.leftText: Stay with me; do not be afraid, for he who seeks your life is seeking mine as well. You will be safe with me.”
units.rightText: Abide thou with me, fear not; for he that seeketh my life seeketh thy life: for with me thou shalt be in safeguard.

units.leftText: Now it was reported to David, “Look, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah and looting the threshing floors.”
units.rightText: And they told David, saying, Behold, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah, and are robbing the threshing-floors.

units.leftText: So David inquired of the LORD, “Should I go and attack these Philistines?” And the LORD said to David, “Go and attack the Philistines and save Keilah.”
units.rightText: Therefore David inquired of Jehovah, saying, Shall I go and smite these Philistines? And Jehovah said unto David, Go, and smite the Philistines, and save Keilah.

units.leftText: But David’s men said to him, “Look, we are afraid here in Judah; how much more if we go to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines?”
units.rightText: And David’s men said unto him, Behold, we are afraid here in Judah: how much more then if we go to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines?

units.leftText: Once again, David inquired of the LORD, and the LORD answered him: “Go at once to Keilah, for I will deliver the Philistines into your hand.”
units.rightText: Then David inquired of Jehovah yet again. And Jehovah answered him, and said, Arise, go down to Keilah; for I will deliver the Philistines into thy hand.

units.leftText: Then David and his men went to Keilah, fought against the Philistines, and carried off their livestock, striking them with a mighty blow. So David saved the people of Keilah.
units.rightText: And David and his men went to Keilah, and fought with the Philistines, and brought away their cattle, and slew them with a great slaughter. So David saved the inhabitants of Keilah.

units.leftText: (Now Abiathar son of Ahimelech had brought the ephod with him when he fled to David at Keilah.) Saul Pursues David (Psalm 54:1–7|PSA 54:1-7*)
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Abiathar the son of Ahimelech fled to David to Keilah, that he came down with an ephod in his hand.

units.leftText: When Saul was told that David had gone to Keilah, he said, “God has delivered him into my hand, for he has trapped himself by entering a town with gates and bars.”
units.rightText: And it was told Saul that David was come to Keilah. And Saul said, God hath delivered him into my hand; for he is shut in, by entering into a town that hath gates and bars.

units.leftText: Then Saul summoned all his troops to go to war at Keilah and besiege David and his men.
units.rightText: And Saul summoned all the people to war, to go down to Keilah, to besiege David and his men.

units.leftText: When David learned that Saul was plotting evil against him, he said to Abiathar the priest, “Bring the ephod.”
units.rightText: And David knew that Saul was devising mischief against him; and he said to Abiathar the priest, Bring hither the ephod.

units.leftText: And David said, “O LORD, God of Israel, Your servant has heard that Saul intends to come to Keilah and destroy the city on my account.
units.rightText: Then said David, O Jehovah, the God of Israel, thy servant hath surely heard that Saul seeketh to come to Keilah, to destroy the city for my sake.

units.leftText: Will the citizens of Keilah surrender me into his hand? Will Saul come down, as Your servant has heard? O LORD, God of Israel, please tell Your servant.” “He will,” said the LORD.
units.rightText: Will the men of Keilah deliver me up into his hand? will Saul come down, as thy servant hath heard? O Jehovah, the God of Israel, I beseech thee, tell thy servant. And Jehovah said, He will come down.
leftNotes: 23:11 Some manuscripts omit this question.

units.leftText: So David asked, “Will the citizens of Keilah surrender me and my men into the hand of Saul?” “They will,” said the LORD.
units.rightText: Then said David, Will the men of Keilah deliver up me and my men into the hand of Saul? And Jehovah said, They will deliver thee up.

units.leftText: Then David and his men, about six hundred strong, set out and departed from Keilah, moving from place to place. When Saul was told that David had escaped from Keilah, he declined to go forth.
units.rightText: Then David and his men, who were about six hundred, arose and departed out of Keilah, and went whithersoever they could go. And it was told Saul that David was escaped from Keilah; and he forbare to go forth.

units.leftText: And David stayed in the wilderness strongholds and in the hill country of the Wilderness of Ziph. Day after day Saul searched for him, but God would not deliver David into his hand.
units.rightText: And David abode in the wilderness in the strongholds, and remained in the hill-country in the wilderness of Ziph. And Saul sought him every day, but God delivered him not into his hand.

units.leftText: While David was in Horesh in the Wilderness of Ziph, he saw that Saul had come out to take his life.
units.rightText: And David saw that Saul was come out to seek his life: and David was in the wilderness of Ziph in the wood.

units.leftText: And Saul’s son Jonathan came to David in Horesh and strengthened his hand in God,
units.rightText: And Jonathan, Saul’s son, arose, and went to David into the wood, and strengthened his hand in God.

units.leftText: saying, “Do not be afraid, for my father Saul will never lay a hand on you. And you will be king over Israel, and I will be your second-in-command. Even my father Saul knows this is true.”
units.rightText: And he said unto him, Fear not; for the hand of Saul my father shall not find thee; and thou shalt be king over Israel, and I shall be next unto thee; and that also Saul my father knoweth.

units.leftText: So the two of them made a covenant before the LORD. And David remained in Horesh, while Jonathan went home.
units.rightText: And they two made a covenant before Jehovah: and David abode in the wood, and Jonathan went to his house.

units.leftText: Then the Ziphites came up to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Is not David hiding among us in the strongholds at Horesh, on the hill of Hachilah south of Jeshimon?
units.rightText: Then came up the Ziphites to Saul to Gibeah, saying, Doth not David hide himself with us in the strongholds in the wood, in the hill of Hachilah, which is on the south of the desert?

units.leftText: Now, O king, come down whenever your soul desires, and we will be responsible for delivering him into your hand.”
units.rightText: Now therefore, O king, come down, according to all the desire of thy soul to come down; and our part shall be to deliver him up into the king’s hand.

units.leftText: “May you be blessed by the LORD,” replied Saul, “for you have had compassion on me.
units.rightText: And Saul said, Blessed be ye of Jehovah; for ye have had compassion on me.

units.leftText: Please go and prepare further. Investigate and watch carefully where he goes and who has seen him there, for I am told that he is extremely cunning.
units.rightText: Go, I pray you, make yet more sure, and know and see his place where his haunt is, and who hath seen him there; for it is told me that he dealeth very subtly.

units.leftText: Observe and find out all the places where he hides. Then come back to me with certainty, and I will go with you. If he is in the land, I will search him out among all the clans of Judah.”
units.rightText: See therefore, and take knowledge of all the lurking-places where he hideth himself, and come ye again to me of a certainty, and I will go with you: and it shall come to pass, if he be in the land, that I will search him out among all the thousands of Judah.

units.leftText: So they set out and went to Ziph ahead of Saul. Now David and his men were in the Wilderness of Maon in the Arabah south of Jeshimon,
units.rightText: And they arose, and went to Ziph before Saul: but David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the Arabah on the south of the desert.

units.leftText: and Saul and his men went to seek him. When David was told about it, he went down to the rock and stayed in the Wilderness of Maon. And when Saul heard of this, he pursued David there.
units.rightText: And Saul and his men went to seek him. And they told David: wherefore he came down to the rock, and abode in the wilderness of Maon. And when Saul heard that, he pursued after David in the wilderness of Maon.

units.leftText: Saul was proceeding along one side of the mountain, and David and his men along the other side. Even though David was hurrying to get away, Saul and his men were closing in on David and his men to capture them.
units.rightText: And Saul went on this side of the mountain, and David and his men on that side of the mountain: and David made haste to get away for fear of Saul; for Saul and his men compassed David and his men round about to take them.

units.leftText: Then a messenger came to Saul, saying, “Come quickly, for the Philistines have raided the land!”
units.rightText: But there came a messenger unto Saul, saying, Haste thee, and come; for the Philistines have made a raid upon the land.

units.leftText: So Saul broke off his pursuit of David and went to meet the Philistines. That is why that place is called Sela-hammahlekoth.
units.rightText: So Saul returned from pursuing after David, and went against the Philistines: therefore they called that place Sela-hammahlekoth.
leftNotes: 23:28 Sela-hammahlekoth means Rock of Escape.

units.leftText: And David went up from there and lived in the strongholds of En-gedi.
units.rightText: And David went up from thence, and dwelt in the strongholds of En-gedi.

units.leftText: After Saul had returned from pursuing the Philistines, he was told, “David is in the wilderness of En-gedi.”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Saul was returned from following the Philistines, that it was told him, saying, Behold, David is in the wilderness of En-gedi.

units.leftText: So Saul took three thousand chosen men from all Israel and went to look for David and his men in the region of the Rocks of the Wild Goats.
units.rightText: Then Saul took three thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and went to seek David and his men upon the rocks of the wild goats.

units.leftText: Soon Saul came to the sheepfolds along the road, where there was a cave, and he went in to relieve himself. And David and his men were hiding in the recesses of the cave.
units.rightText: And he came to the sheepcotes by the way, where was a cave; and Saul went in to cover his feet. Now David and his men were abiding in the innermost parts of the cave.
leftNotes: 24:3 Literally cover his feet, a euphemism for relieving oneself

units.leftText: So David’s men said to him, “This is the day about which the LORD said to you, ‘Behold, I will deliver your enemy into your hand, that you may do with him as you wish.’” Then David crept up and stealthily cut off a corner of Saul’s robe.
units.rightText: And the men of David said unto him, Behold, the day of which Jehovah said unto thee, Behold, I will deliver thine enemy into thy hand, and thou shalt do to him as it shall seem good unto thee. Then David arose, and cut off the skirt of Saul’s robe privily.

units.leftText: Afterward, David’s conscience was stricken because he had cut off the corner of Saul’s robe.
units.rightText: And it came to pass afterward, that David’s heart smote him, because he had cut off Saul’s skirt.

units.leftText: So he said to his men, “The LORD forbid that I should do such a thing to my master, the LORD’s anointed. May I never lift my hand against him, since he is the LORD’s anointed.”
units.rightText: And he said unto his men, Jehovah forbid that I should do this thing unto my lord, Jehovah’s anointed, to put forth my hand against him, seeing he is Jehovah’s anointed.

units.leftText: With these words David restrained his men, and he did not let them rise up against Saul. Then Saul left the cave and went on his way.
units.rightText: So David checked his men with these words, and suffered them not to rise against Saul. And Saul rose up out of the cave, and went on his way.

units.leftText: After that, David got up, went out of the cave, and called out to Saul, “My lord the king!”
units.rightText: David also arose afterward, and went out of the cave, and cried after Saul, saying, My lord the king. And when Saul looked behind him, David bowed with his face to the earth, and did obeisance.

units.leftText: and said to Saul, “Why do you listen to the words of men who say, ‘Look, David intends to harm you’ ?
units.rightText: And David said to Saul, Wherefore hearkenest thou to men’s words, saying, Behold, David seeketh thy hurt?

units.leftText: Behold, this day you have seen with your own eyes that the LORD delivered you into my hand in the cave. I was told to kill you, but I spared you and said, ‘I will not lift my hand against my lord, since he is the LORD’s anointed.’
units.rightText: Behold, this day thine eyes have seen how that Jehovah had delivered thee to-day into my hand in the cave: and some bade me kill thee; but mine eye spared thee; and I said, I will not put forth my hand against my lord; for he is Jehovah’s anointed.

units.leftText: See, my father, look at the corner of your robe in my hand. For I cut it off, but I did not kill you. Know and see that there is no evil or rebellion in my hands. I have not sinned against you, even though you are hunting me down to take my life.
units.rightText: Moreover, my father, see, yea, see the skirt of thy robe in my hand; for in that I cut off the skirt of thy robe, and killed thee not, know thou and see that there is neither evil nor transgression in my hand, and I have not sinned against thee, though thou huntest after my life to take it.

units.leftText: May the LORD judge between you and me, and may the LORD take vengeance on you, but my hand will never be against you.
units.rightText: Jehovah judge between me and thee, and Jehovah avenge me of thee; but my hand shall not be upon thee.

units.leftText: As the old proverb says, ‘Wickedness proceeds from the wicked.’ But my hand will never be against you.
units.rightText: As saith the proverb of the ancients, Out of the wicked cometh forth wickedness; but my hand shall not be upon thee.

units.leftText: Against whom has the king of Israel come out? Whom are you pursuing? A dead dog? A flea?
units.rightText: After whom is the king of Israel come out? after whom dost thou pursue? after a dead dog, after a flea.

units.leftText: May the LORD be our judge and decide between you and me. May He take notice and plead my case and deliver me from your hand.” David’s Oath to Saul
units.rightText: Jehovah therefore be judge, and give sentence between me and thee, and see, and plead my cause, and deliver me out of thy hand.

units.leftText: When David had finished saying these things, Saul called back, “Is that your voice, David my son?”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when David had made an end of speaking these words unto Saul, that Saul said, Is this thy voice, my son David? And Saul lifted up his voice, and wept.

units.leftText: and said to David, “You are more righteous than I, for you have rewarded me with good, though I have rewarded you with evil.
units.rightText: And he said to David, Thou art more righteous than I; for thou hast rendered unto me good, whereas I have rendered unto thee evil.

units.leftText: And you have declared this day how you have treated me well, for when the LORD delivered me into your hand, you did not kill me.
units.rightText: And thou hast declared this day how that thou hast dealt well with me, forasmuch as when Jehovah had delivered me up into thy hand, thou killedst me not.

units.leftText: When a man finds his enemy, does he let him go away unharmed? May the LORD reward you with good for what you have done for me this day.
units.rightText: For if a man find his enemy, will he let him go well away? wherefore Jehovah reward thee good for that which thou hast done unto me this day.

units.leftText: Now I know for sure that you will be king and that the kingdom of Israel will be established in your hands.
units.rightText: And now, behold, I know that thou shalt surely be king, and that the kingdom of Israel shall be established in thy hand.

units.leftText: So now, swear to me by the LORD that you will not cut off my descendants or wipe out my name from my father’s house.”
units.rightText: Swear now therefore unto me by Jehovah, that thou wilt not cut off my seed after me, and that thou wilt not destroy my name out of my father’s house.

units.leftText: So David gave his oath to Saul. Then Saul returned home, but David and his men went up to the stronghold.
units.rightText: And David sware unto Saul. And Saul went home; but David and his men gat them up unto the stronghold.

units.leftText: When Samuel died, all Israel gathered to mourn for him; and they buried him at his home in Ramah. Then David set out and went down to the Wilderness of Paran. David, Nabal, and Abigail
units.rightText: And Samuel died; and all Israel gathered themselves together, and lamented him, and buried him in his house at Ramah. And David arose, and went down to the wilderness of Paran.
leftNotes: 25:1 Hebrew and some LXX manuscripts; other LXX manuscripts Maon

units.leftText: Now there was a man in Maon whose business was in Carmel. He was a very wealthy man with a thousand goats and three thousand sheep, which he was shearing in Carmel.
units.rightText: And there was a man in Maon, whose possessions were in Carmel; and the man was very great, and he had three thousand sheep, and a thousand goats: and he was shearing his sheep in Carmel.

units.leftText: His name was Nabal, and his wife’s name was Abigail. She was an intelligent and beautiful woman, but her husband, a Calebite, was harsh and evil in his dealings.
units.rightText: Now the name of the man was Nabal; and the name of his wife Abigail; and the woman was of good understanding, and of a beautiful countenance: but the man was churlish and evil in his doings; and he was of the house of Caleb.

units.leftText: While David was in the wilderness, he heard that Nabal was shearing sheep.
units.rightText: And David heard in the wilderness that Nabal was shearing his sheep.

units.leftText: So David sent ten young men and instructed them, “Go up to Nabal at Carmel. Greet him in my name
units.rightText: And David sent ten young men, and David said unto the young men, Get you up to Carmel, and go to Nabal, and greet him in my name:

units.leftText: and say to him, ‘Long life to you, and peace to you and to your house and to all that belongs to you.
units.rightText: and thus shall ye say to him that liveth in prosperity, Peace be unto thee, and peace be to thy house, and peace be unto all that thou hast.

units.leftText: Now I hear that it is time for shearing. When your shepherds were with us, we did not harass them, and nothing of theirs was missing the whole time they were in Carmel.
units.rightText: And now I have heard that thou hast shearers: thy shepherds have now been with us, and we did them no hurt, neither was there aught missing unto them, all the while they were in Carmel.

units.leftText: Ask your young men, and they will tell you. So let my young men find favor with you, for we have come on the day of a feast. Please give whatever you can spare to your servants and to your son David.’”
units.rightText: Ask thy young men, and they will tell thee: wherefore let the young men find favor in thine eyes; for we come in a good day: give, I pray thee, whatsoever cometh to thy hand, unto thy servants, and to thy son David.

units.leftText: When David’s young men arrived, they relayed all these words to Nabal on behalf of David. Then they waited.
units.rightText: And when David’s young men came, they spake to Nabal according to all those words in the name of David, and ceased.

units.leftText: But Nabal asked them, “Who is David? Who is this son of Jesse? Many servants these days are breaking away from their masters.
units.rightText: And Nabal answered David’s servants, and said, Who is David? and who is the son of Jesse? there are many servants now-a-days that break away every man from his master.

units.leftText: Why should I take my bread and water and the meat I have slaughtered for my shearers, and give them to these men whose origin I do not know?”
units.rightText: Shall I then take my bread, and my water, and my flesh that I have killed for my shearers, and give it unto men of whom I know not whence they are?

units.leftText: So David’s men turned around and went back, and they relayed to him all these words.
units.rightText: So David’s young men turned on their way, and went back, and came and told him according to all these words.

units.leftText: And David said to his men, “Strap on your swords!” So David and all his men strapped on their swords, and about four hundred men followed David, while two hundred stayed with the supplies.
units.rightText: And David said unto his men, Gird ye on every man his sword. And they girded on every man his sword; and David also girded on his sword: and there went up after David about four hundred men; and two hundred abode by the baggage.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, one of Nabal’s young men informed Nabal’s wife Abigail, “Look, David sent messengers from the wilderness to greet our master, but he screamed at them.
units.rightText: But one of the young men told Abigail, Nabal’s wife, saying, Behold, David sent messengers out of the wilderness to salute our master; and he railed at them.

units.leftText: Yet these men were very good to us. When we were in the field, we were not harassed, and nothing of ours went missing the whole time we lived among them.
units.rightText: But the men were very good unto us, and we were not hurt, neither missed we anything, as long as we went with them, when we were in the fields:

units.leftText: They were a wall around us, both day and night, the whole time we were herding our sheep near them.
units.rightText: they were a wall unto us both by night and by day, all the while we were with them keeping the sheep.

units.leftText: Now consider carefully what you must do, because disaster looms over our master and all his household. For he is such a scoundrel that nobody can speak to him!” Abigail Intercedes for Nabal
units.rightText: Now therefore know and consider what thou wilt do; for evil is determined against our master, and against all his house: for he is such a worthless fellow, that one cannot speak to him.

units.leftText: Then Abigail hurried and took two hundred loaves of bread, two skins of wine, five butchered sheep, five seahs of roasted grain, a hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs. She loaded them on donkeys
units.rightText: Then Abigail made haste, and took two hundred loaves, and two bottles of wine, and five sheep ready dressed, and five measures of parched grain, and a hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs, and laid them on asses.
leftNotes: 25:18 5 seahs is approximately 33 dry quarts or 36.5 liters of roasted grain.

units.leftText: and said to her young men, “Go ahead of me. I will be right behind you.” But she did not tell her husband Nabal.
units.rightText: And she said unto her young men, Go on before me; behold, I come after you. But she told not her husband Nabal.

units.leftText: As Abigail came riding her donkey into a mountain ravine, she saw David and his men coming down toward her, and she met them.
units.rightText: And it was so, as she rode on her ass, and came down by the covert of the mountain, that, behold, David and his men came down toward her; and she met them.

units.leftText: Now David had just said, “In vain I have protected all that belonged to this man in the wilderness. Nothing that belongs to him has gone missing, yet he has paid me back evil for good.
units.rightText: Now David had said, Surely in vain have I kept all that this fellow hath in the wilderness, so that nothing was missed of all that pertained unto him: and he hath returned me evil for good.

units.leftText: May God punish David, and ever so severely, if I let one male belonging to Nabal survive until morning.”
units.rightText: God do so unto the enemies of David, and more also, if I leave of all that pertain to him by the morning light so much as one man-child.
leftNotes: 25:22 Some LXX manuscripts; MT David’s enemies

units.leftText: When Abigail saw David, she quickly got off the donkey, fell facedown, and bowed before him.
units.rightText: And when Abigail saw David, she hasted, and alighted from her ass, and fell before David on her face, and bowed herself to the ground.

units.leftText: She fell at his feet and said, “My lord, may the blame be on me alone, but please let your servant speak to you; hear the words of your servant.
units.rightText: And she fell at his feet, and said, Upon me, my lord, upon me be the iniquity; and let thy handmaid, I pray thee, speak in thine ears, and hear thou the words of thy handmaid.

units.leftText: My lord should pay no attention to this scoundrel Nabal, for he lives up to his name: His name means Fool, and folly accompanies him. I, your servant, did not see my lord’s young men whom you sent.
units.rightText: Let not my lord, I pray thee, regard this worthless fellow, even Nabal; for as his name is, so is he; Nabal is his name, and folly is with him: but I thy handmaid saw not the young men of my lord, whom thou didst send.
leftNotes: 25:25 Nabal means fool.

units.leftText: Now, my lord, as surely as the LORD lives and you yourself live, since the LORD has held you back from bloodshed and from avenging yourself with your own hand, may your enemies and those who seek harm for my lord be like Nabal.
units.rightText: Now therefore, my lord, as Jehovah liveth, and as thy soul liveth, seeing Jehovah hath withholden thee from bloodguiltiness, and from avenging thyself with thine own hand, now therefore let thine enemies, and them that seek evil to my lord, be as Nabal.

units.leftText: Now let this gift your servant has brought to my lord be given to the young men who follow you.
units.rightText: And now this present which thy servant hath brought unto my lord, let it be given unto the young men that follow my lord.

units.leftText: Please forgive your servant’s offense, for the LORD will surely make a lasting dynasty for my lord, because he fights the LORD’s battles. May no evil be found in you as long as you live.
units.rightText: Forgive, I pray thee, the trespass of thy handmaid: for Jehovah will certainly make my lord a sure house, because my lord fighteth the battles of Jehovah; and evil shall not be found in thee all thy days.

units.leftText: And should someone pursue you and seek your life, then the life of my lord will be bound securely by the LORD your God in the bundle of the living. But He shall fling away the lives of your enemies like stones from a sling.
units.rightText: And though men be risen up to pursue thee, and to seek thy soul, yet the soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life with Jehovah thy God; and the souls of thine enemies, them shall he sling out, as from the hollow of a sling.
leftNotes: 25:29 Literally fling away the souls of your enemies as from the pocket of a sling

units.leftText: When the LORD has done for my lord all the good He promised, and when He has appointed you ruler over Israel,
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, when Jehovah shall have done to my lord according to all the good that he hath spoken concerning thee, and shall have appointed thee prince over Israel,

units.leftText: then my lord will have no remorse or guilt of conscience over needless bloodshed and revenge. And when the LORD has dealt well with my lord, may you remember your servant.”
units.rightText: that this shall be no grief unto thee, nor offence of heart unto my lord, either that thou hast shed blood without cause, or that my lord hath avenged himself. And when Jehovah shall have dealt well with my lord, then remember thy handmaid.

units.leftText: Then David said to Abigail, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who sent you to meet me this day!
units.rightText: And David said to Abigail, Blessed be Jehovah, the God of Israel, who sent thee this day to meet me:

units.leftText: Blessed is your discernment, and blessed are you, because today you kept me from bloodshed and from avenging myself by my own hand.
units.rightText: and blessed be thy discretion, and blessed be thou, that hast kept me this day from bloodguiltiness, and from avenging myself with mine own hand.

units.leftText: Otherwise, as surely as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, who has restrained me from harming you, if you had not come quickly to meet me, then surely no male belonging to Nabal would have been left alive by morning light.”
units.rightText: For in very deed, as Jehovah, the God of Israel, liveth, who hath withholden me from hurting thee, except thou hadst hasted and come to meet me, surely there had not been left unto Nabal by the morning light so much as one man-child.

units.leftText: Then David accepted from her hand what she had brought him, and he said to her, “Go home in peace. See, I have heeded your voice and granted your request.”
units.rightText: So David received of her hand that which she had brought him: and he said unto her, Go up in peace to thy house; see, I have hearkened to thy voice, and have accepted thy person.

units.leftText: When Abigail returned to Nabal, there he was in the house, holding a feast fit for a king, in high spirits and very drunk. So she told him nothing until morning light.
units.rightText: And Abigail came to Nabal; and, behold, he held a feast in his house, like the feast of a king; and Nabal’s heart was merry within him, for he was very drunken: wherefore she told him nothing, less or more, until the morning light.

units.leftText: In the morning when Nabal was sober, his wife told him about these events, and his heart failed within him, and he became like a stone.
units.rightText: And it came to pass in the morning, when the wine was gone out of Nabal, that his wife told him these things, and his heart died within him, and he became as a stone.

units.leftText: About ten days later, the LORD struck Nabal dead. David Marries Abigail
units.rightText: And it came to pass about ten days after, that Jehovah smote Nabal, so that he died.

units.leftText: On hearing that Nabal was dead, David said, “Blessed be the LORD, who has upheld my cause against the reproach of Nabal and has restrained His servant from evil. For the LORD has brought the wickedness of Nabal down upon his own head.”
units.rightText: And when David heard that Nabal was dead, he said, Blessed be Jehovah, that hath pleaded the cause of my reproach from the hand of Nabal, and hath kept back his servant from evil: and the evil-doing of Nabal hath Jehovah returned upon his own head. And David sent and spake concerning Abigail, to take her to him to wife.
